questions.text: Which source document is used to record a credit sale?

options: unusual items such as corrections and opening entries

questions.text: Which document supports an entry for a small payment from petty cash?
questions.explanation: Each petty payment should have a signed voucher.

questions.text: A debit note is sent by a buyer to a supplier to
options: claim a reduction for goods returned or overcharges
questions.explanation: The supplier responds with a credit note.

questions.text: The book of original entry for credit purchases of goods is the
questions.explanation: Only credit purchases of goods for resale go into it.

questions.text: Accounts of debtors are kept in the
questions.explanation: Each credit customer has a personal account.

questions.text: Accounts of expenses and incomes, such as rent and commission, are

questions.text: An account for machinery is a
questions.explanation: Real accounts record assets.

questions.text: A debit balance on a customer's account means the customer

questions.text: The balance brought down at the start of a new period is shown as

questions.text: Rent paid by cheque is recorded as
questions.explanation: The expense increases (debit) and the bank balance falls (credit).

questions.text: The account into which all federal government revenue is paid is the
questions.explanation: Spending from it requires approval by the legislature.

questions.text: The officer responsible for auditing federal government accounts is the

questions.text: The officer responsible for the accounts and payments of the federal government is the
questions.explanation: The Accountant-General prepares government accounts.

questions.text: Public sector accounting differs from private accounting mainly because it focuses on
options: accountability for public funds rather than profit
questions.explanation: Governments must account for how public money is spent.

questions.text: A document showing the government's estimated revenue and spending for a year is the
questions.explanation: The Appropriation Act authorises the spending.

questions.text: Which fund is set aside to repay a long-term loan when it falls due?
questions.explanation: Regular amounts are invested so the loan can be repaid.

questions.text: The current ratio is calculated as
questions.explanation: It shows a firm's ability to pay short-term debts.

Working capital is
questions.explanation: It is the money available for day-to-day operations.

questions.text: Rate of stock turnover is calculated as
questions.explanation: It shows how many times stock is sold in a period.

questions.text: The quick (acid test) ratio excludes which item from current assets?
questions.explanation: Stock may not be quickly turned into cash.

questions.text: The accounting concept that requires expenses to be matched with the revenue they help earn is
questions.explanation: Expenses are recorded in the period in which the related income is earned.

questions.text: Only transactions that can be expressed in money are recorded. This is the
questions.explanation: Staff morale, for example, cannot be recorded in the books.

questions.text: The people who use accounting information include
questions.explanation: Many groups rely on financial statements.

questions.text: Bookkeeping is the
questions.explanation: Bookkeeping records transactions so that accounts can be prepared.

questions.text: The accounting equation is
questions.explanation: Everything the business owns is financed by the owner (capital) or by outsiders (liabilities).

questions.text: A business has assets of ₦500,000 and liabilities of ₦200,000. What is its capital?
questions.explanation: Capital = Assets − Liabilities = 500,000 − 200,000 = ₦300,000.

questions.text: Which of these is a liability?
questions.explanation: A liability is an amount the business owes to outsiders.

questions.text: The concept that a business is treated separately from its owner is the
questions.explanation: The owner's private affairs are kept separate from the business records.

questions.text: Which concept assumes that a business will continue operating for the foreseeable future?
questions.explanation: Assets are valued on the basis that the business will keep running.

questions.text: The double entry principle states that every transaction has
options: a debit entry and a corresponding credit entry
questions.explanation: For every debit there is an equal credit.

questions.text: When a business buys goods for cash, the entries are
questions.explanation: Purchases increase (debit) and cash decreases (credit).

questions.text: When goods are sold on credit to Ada, the entries are
questions.explanation: Ada becomes a debtor (debit) and sales increase (credit).

questions.text: The owner brings ₦100,000 cash into the business. The entries are
questions.explanation: Cash increases (debit) and the owner's capital increases (credit).

questions.text: Goods taken by the owner for personal use are recorded as
questions.explanation: Drawings reduce capital; the goods are removed from purchases.

questions.text: Which book of original entry records credit purchases of goods?
questions.explanation: Credit purchases are first entered in the purchases day book.

questions.text: A cash book that records cash, bank and discount columns is a
questions.explanation: The three columns are discount, cash and bank.

questions.text: In the cash book, discount allowed appears on the
questions.explanation: Discount allowed is given to customers who pay, so it sits with the receipts on the debit side.

questions.text: The petty cash system in which the cashier is refunded the amount spent is the
questions.explanation: Under the imprest system, the float is restored to the same amount at the end of each period.

questions.text: A petty cashier has an imprest of ₦20,000 and spends ₦14,500. How much should be reimbursed?
questions.explanation: Under the imprest system, the amount spent is reimbursed to restore the float.

questions.text: A contra entry in the cash book occurs when
options: cash is paid into the bank or withdrawn from the bank for office use
questions.explanation: Both sides of the entry are in the cash book (cash and bank columns).

questions.text: Petty cash is used for
questions.explanation: Examples include postage, transport fares and cleaning materials.

questions.text: A trial balance is prepared to
options: show the profit for the year
check the arithmetical accuracy of the ledger
questions.explanation: If the debit and credit totals agree, the double entry is arithmetically correct.

questions.text: Which error will NOT be revealed by a trial balance?
options: entering only the debit side of a transaction
entering different amounts on the debit and credit sides
adding a column wrongly on one side
questions.explanation: If a transaction is left out completely, both sides are still equal.

questions.text: Recording a payment to Musa in Moses's account is an
questions.explanation: The right type of account, but the wrong person's account.

questions.text: Recording the purchase of a motor van in the purchases account is an
questions.explanation: A fixed asset has been treated as a revenue item.

questions.text: An account opened to make the trial balance agree temporarily is a
questions.explanation: The difference is placed in a suspense account until the errors are found.

questions.text: Which balance normally appears on the debit side of the trial balance?
questions.explanation: Expenses, assets and purchases have debit balances.

questions.text: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared to
options: explain the difference between the cash book and the bank statement balances
questions.explanation: Timing differences and errors cause the two balances to differ.

questions.text: Cheques written and sent to suppliers but not yet presented at the bank are
questions.explanation: The cash book shows the payment, but the bank has not yet paid it.

questions.text: Bank charges shown on the bank statement but not in the cash book should be
questions.explanation: Charges reduce the bank balance, so they are credited in the cash book.

questions.text: Cheques paid into the bank but not yet credited by the bank are
questions.explanation: They appear in the cash book but not yet on the bank statement.

questions.text: A customer's cheque that the bank refuses to pay is a
questions.explanation: The amount must be credited in the cash book and debited back to the customer.

questions.text: Interest received from the bank that is not yet in the cash book should be
questions.explanation: Interest received increases the bank balance.

questions.text: Opening stock ₦20,000, purchases ₦80,000 and closing stock ₦15,000. What is the cost of sales?
Sales are ₦150,000 and cost of sales is ₦90,000. What is the gross profit?
questions.explanation: Gross profit = sales − cost of sales = ₦60,000.

questions.text: Gross profit is ₦60,000 and expenses are ₦25,000. What is the net profit?
questions.explanation: Net profit = gross profit − expenses = ₦35,000.

questions.text: Which statement shows the assets, liabilities and capital of a business on a particular date?
questions.explanation: The balance sheet is a snapshot of the business's financial position.

questions.text: Carriage inwards is charged to the
options: profit and loss account as a selling expense
questions.explanation: Carriage inwards adds to the cost of purchases.

questions.text: Which of these is a current asset?
questions.explanation: Current assets are expected to turn into cash within a year.

questions.text: Rent owing at the end of the year is an example of
questions.explanation: The expense belongs to this year but has not yet been paid.

questions.text: Insurance paid in advance for next year is shown in the balance sheet as a
questions.explanation: A prepayment is an amount the business is owed in services.

questions.text: A machine costs ₦100,000, will last 5 years and has no scrap value. What is the yearly straight-line depreciation?
questions.explanation: Depreciation = (cost − scrap value) ÷ useful life = 100,000 ÷ 5 = ₦20,000.

questions.text: A van costing ₦400,000 is depreciated at 10% a year on the reducing balance method. What is the depreciation in year 2?
A provision for doubtful debts is created in line with the
questions.explanation: Prudence means expected losses are recognised as soon as they are foreseen.

questions.text: Depreciation is best described as
options: the profit on selling an asset
an increase in the value of land
the loss in value of a non-current asset over its useful life
cash set aside to buy new assets
questions.explanation: It spreads the cost of the asset over the years it is used.

questions.text: The sales ledger control account is also called the
questions.explanation: It summarises all the individual debtors' accounts.

questions.text: Which item appears on the credit side of the sales ledger control account?
questions.explanation: Cash received reduces what debtors owe, so it is credited.

questions.text: A statement of affairs is prepared to find the
options: capital of a business with incomplete records
questions.explanation: Capital = assets − liabilities on a given date.

questions.text: Opening capital ₦200,000, closing capital ₦260,000, drawings ₦30,000 and no new capital. What is the profit?
questions.explanation: Profit = closing capital − opening capital + drawings = 60,000 + 30,000 = ₦90,000.

questions.text: Which item appears on the debit side of the purchases ledger control account?
questions.explanation: Payments reduce what is owed to creditors, so they are debited.

questions.text: Single entry is a system of bookkeeping in which
options: no records are kept at all
transactions are not fully recorded by double entry
questions.explanation: Small traders often keep incomplete records, mainly of cash and personal accounts.

questions.text: If there is no partnership agreement, profits are shared
questions.explanation: Under the Partnership Act, profits and losses are shared equally when there is no agreement.

questions.text: Interest on drawings is
options: charged to partners and added to profit available for sharing
an expense in the trading account
questions.explanation: It discourages partners from making large drawings.

questions.text: Partners A and B share profits in the ratio 3:2. Profit is ₦50,000. What is B's share?
The account that shows how partnership profit is shared is the
questions.explanation: It deals with salaries, interest on capital and the sharing of the residual profit.

questions.text: Goodwill is
options: the value of a business's reputation and customer connections
questions.explanation: Goodwill is an intangible asset.

questions.text: The account opened when a partnership is dissolved is the
questions.explanation: Assets are sold and liabilities settled through the realisation account.

questions.text: The amount of share capital a company is permitted to issue is its
questions.explanation: It is stated in the memorandum of association.

questions.text: A company's undistributed profits kept in the business are
questions.explanation: Retained earnings belong to the ordinary shareholders.

questions.text: Direct materials ₦50,000, direct labour ₦30,000 and direct expenses ₦5,000. What is the prime cost?
questions.explanation: Prime cost = direct materials + direct labour + direct expenses.

questions.text: Factory rent is part of
questions.explanation: Indirect factory costs are added to prime cost to give cost of production.

questions.text: Receipts and payments accounts are prepared by
questions.explanation: Clubs summarise cash received and paid in a receipts and payments account.

questions.text: In a not-for-profit organisation, an excess of income over expenditure is called a
questions.explanation: Clubs do not aim to make profit, so the term "surplus" is used.

questions.text: Which factor most affects the availability of land for farming in Nigerian cities?
questions.explanation: Growing towns take over land that could be farmed.

questions.text: The Land Use Act of 1978 vests land in each state in the
questions.explanation: The Governor holds land in trust for the people of the state.

questions.text: Which is a non-agricultural use of land?
questions.explanation: Land is also used for housing, industry, transport and recreation.

questions.text: Land left uncultivated for some years to regain fertility is
questions.explanation: Bush fallowing lets natural vegetation restore the soil.

questions.text: Which land tenure system allows a farmer to use land in exchange for regular payments?
questions.explanation: The tenant pays rent to the owner for use of the land.

questions.text: A disadvantage of the inheritance system of land ownership is
options: fragmentation of land into small plots
questions.explanation: Sharing land among many heirs leaves each with tiny, scattered plots.

questions.text: Propagation using seeds is called
questions.explanation: Seeds result from fertilisation.

questions.text: Joining a shoot (scion) of one plant to the rootstock of another is
questions.explanation: Grafting is used for citrus and mango.

questions.text: Bending a branch into the soil so that it forms roots before it is cut off is
questions.explanation: Layering is used for plants such as hibiscus.

questions.text: Removing excess seedlings to give the rest space to grow is called
questions.explanation: Thinning reduces competition among seedlings.

questions.text: Replacing seeds that failed to germinate is called
questions.explanation: Supplying keeps the plant population at the right level.

questions.text: Covering the soil surface with dry grass or leaves is called
questions.explanation: Mulch conserves moisture, controls weeds and reduces erosion.

questions.text: Supplying water to crops artificially is called
questions.explanation: Irrigation allows farming in the dry season.

questions.text: Removing excess water from waterlogged land is called
questions.explanation: Drainage improves soil aeration for roots.

questions.text: Which irrigation method delivers water slowly to the base of each plant?
questions.explanation: Drip irrigation saves water.

questions.text: Which crop is commonly grown with irrigation in river valleys of northern Nigeria (fadama)?
questions.explanation: Fadama lands are flood plains used for dry-season farming.

questions.text: A problem caused by poor irrigation management is
questions.explanation: Evaporating irrigation water can leave salts behind.

questions.text: Which is an advantage of irrigation?
options: crops can be grown all year round
questions.explanation: Irrigation removes dependence on seasonal rainfall.

questions.text: Chickens raised mainly for meat are called
questions.explanation: Broilers grow fast and are ready for sale in about 6–8 weeks.

questions.text: Chickens raised mainly for eggs are called
questions.explanation: Layers begin laying at about 18–20 weeks.

questions.text: The system in which poultry are kept in cages is the
questions.explanation: Cages make egg collection easy and reduce disease spread.

questions.text: In the deep litter system, poultry are kept
options: on the floor of a house covered with wood shavings
questions.explanation: Litter absorbs moisture from droppings.

questions.text: A young female chicken that has not started laying is a
questions.explanation: A cockerel is a young male chicken.

questions.text: The process of heating eggs artificially to hatch them is
questions.explanation: Candling checks eggs against a light to see if they are fertile.

questions.text: Which feed component is mainly for body building in farm animals?
questions.explanation: Proteins build muscles and tissues.

questions.text: Which of these is a concentrate feed?
questions.explanation: Concentrates are rich in nutrients and low in fibre.

questions.text: Grass preserved in a moist state by fermentation is called
questions.explanation: Silage is stored in airtight silos.

questions.text: Grass cut and dried for storage is called
questions.explanation: Hay is fed to animals in the dry season.

questions.text: A ration that contains all nutrients in the right proportions is a
questions.explanation: Balanced rations meet an animal's full needs.

questions.text: Which mineral deficiency causes milk fever in dairy cows?
questions.explanation: Milk fever occurs when blood calcium drops after calving.

questions.text: Which is a source of farm power?
questions.explanation: Sources include human labour, animals, tractors, wind and electricity.

questions.text: Using animals such as oxen to pull ploughs is called
questions.explanation: Animal traction is common in northern Nigeria.

questions.text: Which is a limitation of farm mechanisation in Nigeria?
options: high cost of machines and spare parts
questions.explanation: Small, scattered farms and costs limit machine use.

questions.text: A combine harvester is used to
questions.explanation: It cuts the crop and separates the grain at once.

questions.text: Which implement is used for planting seeds in rows?
questions.explanation: Planters place seeds at the right depth and spacing.

questions.text: Which practice keeps farm machinery in good condition?
questions.explanation: Maintenance prevents breakdowns.

questions.text: Which crop is a fibre crop?
questions.explanation: Cotton fibre is used for textiles.

questions.text: Rice is best grown in
questions.explanation: Lowland rice needs standing water.

questions.text: Which crop is a legume?
questions.explanation: Groundnut, cowpea and soybean are legumes.

questions.text: The harvesting of cocoa involves cutting the
questions.explanation: Ripe pods are cut and the beans are fermented and dried.

questions.text: Which insect pest is known to destroy farms in swarms?
questions.explanation: Desert locusts can destroy crops over large areas.

questions.text: Weeds harm crops mainly by
options: competing for light, water and nutrients
questions.explanation: Weeds reduce yields through competition.

questions.text: Which of these is a cultural method of weed control?
options: burning the whole farm each week
questions.explanation: Cultural methods change farming practices to reduce weeds.

questions.text: The young of a goat is called a
questions.explanation: A young sheep is a lamb; a young cow is a calf.

questions.text: The act of giving birth in pigs is called
questions.explanation: Goats kid, cattle calve and sheep lamb.

questions.text: Which animal is a monogastric (non-ruminant)?
questions.explanation: Pigs have a simple stomach.

questions.text: Which of these is a major importance of agriculture to Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Agriculture feeds the population and employs a large share of workers.

questions.text: Farming in which the farmer produces mainly to feed the family is
questions.explanation: Subsistence farmers produce little surplus for sale.

questions.text: Which of these is a problem facing agriculture in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Many smallholder farmers cannot get loans for inputs and equipment.

questions.text: Shifting cultivation is a system in which
options: the farmer moves to a new piece of land when the soil loses fertility
crops are grown in the same field every year
questions.explanation: The old land is left to regain its fertility naturally.

questions.text: Growing two or more crops on the same piece of land at the same time is
questions.explanation: Mixed cropping spreads risk and makes good use of land.

questions.text: Growing different crops on the same land in a planned sequence over seasons is
questions.explanation: Crop rotation helps maintain fertility and control pests and diseases.

questions.text: Which farm tool is used for clearing grass and bush?
questions.explanation: The cutlass (machete) is used to clear vegetation.

questions.text: Which tractor implement is used for primary tillage?
questions.explanation: Ploughing is the first tillage operation; harrowing breaks the clods afterwards.

questions.text: Which implement is used to break up clods after ploughing?
questions.explanation: Harrowing is secondary tillage that gives a fine tilth.

questions.text: Which tool is used to spray chemicals on crops?
questions.explanation: The knapsack sprayer is carried on the back and pumped by hand.

questions.text: Which of these is a routine maintenance practice for farm tools?
questions.explanation: Cleaning and oiling prevent rust and prolong their life.

questions.text: Which machine is used for making ridges on a large farm?
questions.explanation: A tractor-drawn ridger forms ridges for crops such as yam and cassava.

questions.text: Which type of soil is best for most crops?
questions.explanation: Loam holds water well, drains well and is rich in nutrients.

questions.text: Sandy soil is described as
options: well drained but poor at holding water
questions.explanation: Large particles leave big pore spaces, so water drains quickly.

questions.text: Soil texture refers to
options: the proportion of sand, silt and clay in the soil
questions.explanation: Texture depends on the sizes of the mineral particles.

questions.text: Decayed plant and animal matter in the soil is called
questions.explanation: Humus improves soil structure, water retention and fertility.

questions.text: Which is a method of soil conservation?
questions.explanation: Cover crops protect the soil from rain splash and erosion.

questions.text: Which organism improves soil aeration by burrowing?
questions.explanation: Earthworms make tunnels that let air and water into the soil.

questions.text: Which nutrient mainly promotes leafy growth in plants?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is needed for proteins and chlorophyll, giving green, leafy growth.

questions.text: Which nutrient is especially important for root development?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus helps root growth and early development.

questions.text: The letters NPK on a fertiliser bag stand for
questions.explanation: NPK fertilisers supply the three major nutrients.

questions.text: Lime is added to soil to
questions.explanation: Liming raises the pH of acidic soils.

questions.text: Which of these is an organic manure?
questions.explanation: Organic manures come from plant and animal remains.

questions.text: Which crop adds nitrogen to the soil through its root nodules?
questions.explanation: Legumes such as cowpea host nitrogen-fixing bacteria in their root nodules.

questions.text: Cassava is propagated mainly by
questions.explanation: Cassava stems are cut into pieces and planted.

questions.text: Yam is propagated by
questions.explanation: Pieces of yam tuber are planted to grow new plants.

questions.text: Maize is classified as a
questions.explanation: Cereals are grasses grown for their grains, like maize, rice and sorghum.

questions.text: Which crop is a beverage crop?
questions.explanation: Cocoa, coffee and tea are beverage crops.

questions.text: Plantain and banana are propagated by
questions.explanation: Suckers grow from the base of the parent plant.

questions.text: Which of these is an oil crop?
questions.explanation: The oil palm produces palm oil and palm kernel oil.

questions.text: Cassava mosaic disease is caused by a
questions.explanation: It is spread by whiteflies and infected cuttings.

questions.text: Black pod disease of cocoa is caused by a
questions.explanation: Phytophthora fungus causes cocoa pods to rot and turn black.

questions.text: The vector of groundnut rosette disease is the
questions.explanation: Aphids carry the rosette virus from plant to plant.

questions.text: Which of these is a biological method of pest control?
options: using natural enemies of the pest
questions.explanation: Biological control uses predators, parasites or diseases of the pest.

questions.text: Chemicals used to kill weeds are called
questions.explanation: Herbicides control weeds. Insecticides kill insects and fungicides kill fungi.

questions.text: Which pest attacks stored grains such as maize and beans?
questions.explanation: Weevils bore into and damage stored grains.

questions.text: Which cattle breed is tolerant to trypanosomiasis?
questions.explanation: N'Dama cattle can survive in tsetse-infested areas.

questions.text: A castrated male cattle is called a
questions.explanation: Castrated males are kept for meat or work.

questions.text: An adult female pig is called a
questions.explanation: A sow has given birth. A gilt is a young female that has not yet farrowed.

questions.text: How long does it take a chicken egg to hatch?
questions.explanation: Chicken eggs hatch after about 21 days of incubation.

questions.text: Ruminant animals such as cattle have a stomach with
questions.explanation: The four parts are the rumen, reticulum, omasum and abomasum.

questions.text: Which goat breed is common in northern Nigeria and is known for good skin quality?
questions.explanation: The Red Sokoto (Maradi) goat's skin is valued for leather.

questions.text: Newcastle disease affects mainly
questions.explanation: Newcastle disease is a viral disease of birds.

questions.text: Coccidiosis in poultry is caused by
questions.explanation: Eimeria protozoa damage the intestines and cause bloody droppings.

questions.text: Trypanosomiasis in cattle is spread by the
questions.explanation: The tsetse fly carries trypanosomes.

questions.text: Which of these is a sign of ill health in farm animals?
questions.explanation: Sick animals often stop eating and become dull.

questions.text: Vaccinating animals helps to
questions.explanation: Vaccines build immunity before infection.

questions.text: Ticks are examples of
questions.explanation: Ticks feed on blood from the outside of the body.

questions.text: Young fish stocked in a fish pond are called
questions.explanation: Fingerlings are young fish about the size of a finger.

questions.text: Which fish is commonly farmed in Nigerian ponds?
questions.explanation: Catfish and tilapia are the most widely farmed fish in Nigeria.

questions.text: Growing food crops between young forest trees in the early years of a plantation is the
questions.explanation: Farmers tend the trees while using the space for food crops.

questions.text: Which tree is a valuable timber species in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Iroko is a hardwood used for furniture and construction.

questions.text: Replanting trees in a forest that has been cut down is
questions.explanation: Reafforestation restores forest cover.

questions.text: Which of these is a method of preserving fish?
options: leaving it uncovered at room temperature
questions.explanation: Smoking, drying, salting and freezing are common methods.

questions.text: A record of all the farm's assets such as tools and buildings is the
questions.explanation: An inventory lists the farm's property and its value.

questions.text: The farmer's daily record of activities on the farm is the
questions.explanation: The diary notes operations such as planting, spraying and harvesting.

questions.text: Agricultural extension services are mainly concerned with
options: passing new farming knowledge to farmers
questions.explanation: Extension workers teach farmers about improved methods and research results.

questions.text: The law of diminishing returns states that as more units of a variable input are added to a fixed input,
questions.explanation: For example, adding more labour to a fixed farm eventually adds less and less output.

questions.text: Which of these is a problem of agricultural marketing in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Poor storage leads to waste and forces farmers to sell at low prices.

questions.text: A cooperative society helps farmers by
options: pooling resources to buy inputs and sell produce
questions.explanation: Cooperatives give farmers bargaining power and access to credit.

questions.text: Which is the correct order of organisation from simplest to most complex?
questions.explanation: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form systems, and systems make up the organism.

questions.text: A group of similar cells performing the same function is a
questions.explanation: For example, muscle tissue is made of muscle cells working together.

questions.text: Which of these is an organ?
questions.explanation: An organ is made of several tissues working together. Blood is a tissue; the circulatory system is an organ system.

questions.text: Volvox is an example of organisms living as a
questions.explanation: Volvox cells live together in a colony but each can survive on its own.

questions.text: Which organism is unicellular?
questions.explanation: Amoeba is made of only one cell. Spirogyra is filamentous; Hydra and the earthworm are multicellular.

questions.text: Which is a disadvantage of being a large multicellular organism?
options: cells deep inside the body cannot get materials by diffusion alone
questions.explanation: Large organisms need transport systems because diffusion is too slow over long distances.

questions.text: Which part of a plant absorbs water and mineral salts from the soil?
questions.explanation: Root hairs give a large surface area for absorbing water and minerals.

questions.text: A plant with parallel leaf veins and a fibrous root system is a
questions.explanation: Monocots such as maize and grasses have parallel veins and fibrous roots.

questions.text: A plant with net veins and a tap root system is a
questions.explanation: Dicots such as beans and mango have net-veined leaves and a main tap root.

questions.text: The point on a stem where a leaf is attached is the
questions.explanation: The section of stem between two nodes is the internode.

questions.text: Which modified stem stores food underground?
questions.explanation: An Irish potato is a stem tuber; it has nodes ("eyes"). Carrot is a root.

questions.text: The flat, broad part of a leaf is called the
questions.explanation: The lamina provides a large surface for photosynthesis.

questions.text: Which process returns carbon dioxide to the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Respiration, burning and decay release carbon dioxide; photosynthesis removes it.

questions.text: The conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into nitrogen compounds by bacteria is called
questions.explanation: Bacteria such as Rhizobium in legume nodules fix nitrogen.

questions.text: Bacteria that convert nitrates back into nitrogen gas carry out
questions.explanation: Denitrifying bacteria live in waterlogged, poorly aerated soil.

questions.text: Which bacteria convert ammonium compounds into nitrites?
questions.explanation: Nitrosomonas makes nitrites; Nitrobacter then converts nitrites to nitrates.

questions.text: In the water cycle, water vapour turning into droplets in the clouds is
questions.explanation: Cooling water vapour condenses to form clouds.

questions.text: Lightning helps the nitrogen cycle by
options: removing nitrogen from the air permanently
combining nitrogen and oxygen to form oxides that dissolve in rain
questions.explanation: The energy of lightning makes nitrogen oxides, which form nitrates in the soil.

questions.text: Which reagent is used to test for reducing sugars?
questions.explanation: On heating, a brick-red precipitate shows a reducing sugar such as glucose.

questions.text: Which reagent turns violet (purple) in the presence of protein?
questions.explanation: The Biuret test gives a violet colour with proteins.

questions.text: Which test is used for fats and oils?
questions.explanation: Fat leaves a translucent spot on paper. Sudan III also stains fat red.

questions.text: Enzymes are made of
questions.explanation: Enzymes are protein catalysts, which is why high temperatures denature them.

questions.text: Why do most enzymes stop working at high temperatures?
questions.explanation: Heat changes the shape of the enzyme's active site permanently.

questions.text: Pepsin works best in
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid in the stomach gives pepsin the low pH it needs.

questions.text: Which of these is a useful activity of microorganisms?
questions.explanation: Bacteria make yoghurt and yeast makes bread rise.

questions.text: Which organism is used in brewing and baking?
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide.

questions.text: Which of these is a viral disease?
questions.explanation: HIV is a virus. TB and cholera are bacterial; ringworm is a fungal infection.

questions.text: Antibiotics are used to treat infections caused by
questions.explanation: Antibiotics kill bacteria or stop them growing. They do not work against viruses.

questions.text: The process of heating milk to kill harmful microorganisms is called
questions.explanation: Named after Louis Pasteur, it kills most germs without boiling the milk.

questions.text: Ringworm of the skin is caused by a
questions.explanation: Despite its name, ringworm is a fungal infection.

questions.text: Which part of the eye controls the amount of light entering it?
questions.explanation: The iris changes the size of the pupil.

questions.text: Light-sensitive cells in the eye are found in the
questions.explanation: Rods and cones in the retina detect light.

questions.text: Short-sightedness can be corrected with
questions.explanation: In short sight, light focuses in front of the retina; a concave lens spreads it out first.

questions.text: Which part of the ear is concerned with balance?
questions.explanation: Fluid in the semicircular canals detects movement of the head.

questions.text: The three small bones of the middle ear are called the
questions.explanation: The hammer, anvil and stirrup pass vibrations from the eardrum to the inner ear.

questions.text: Which cells in the retina are responsible for colour vision?
questions.explanation: Cones work in bright light and detect colour; rods work in dim light.

questions.text: Which of these is an abiotic factor?
questions.explanation: Abiotic factors are non-living: temperature, light, rainfall, pH and so on.

questions.text: Which of these is a biotic factor?
questions.explanation: Biotic factors come from living things.

questions.text: Which instrument is used to measure the intensity of light in a habitat?
questions.explanation: A light meter measures how bright it is.

questions.text: A quadrat is used to
options: estimate the number of plants in an area
questions.explanation: A quadrat is a square frame placed at random to sample organisms.

questions.text: Which method is used to estimate the population of moving animals such as grasshoppers?
questions.explanation: The number marked and recaptured is used to estimate the total population.

questions.text: Which habitat is described as aquatic?
questions.explanation: Aquatic habitats are water habitats, either fresh water or marine.

questions.text: Which pollutant is released mainly from car exhausts?
questions.explanation: Incomplete burning of fuel in engines produces carbon monoxide.

questions.text: Excess fertiliser washed into lakes causes rapid algae growth. This is called
questions.explanation: When the algae die, decomposers use up the oxygen and fish die.

questions.text: Which disease is linked to drinking water contaminated by sewage?
questions.explanation: Typhoid bacteria spread through food and water contaminated by faeces.

questions.text: Noise pollution can lead to
questions.explanation: Long exposure to loud noise damages the inner ear.

questions.text: Which is a good way to reduce land pollution by plastics?
questions.explanation: The 3Rs reduce the waste that reaches the environment.

questions.text: Lead in the environment is harmful mainly because it
questions.explanation: Lead is a toxic heavy metal that harms the brain and nerves, especially in children.

questions.text: Which blood group is called the universal donor?
questions.explanation: Group O blood has no A or B antigens on its red cells.

questions.text: Which blood group is called the universal recipient?
questions.explanation: Group AB plasma has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies.

questions.text: The liquid part of the blood is called
questions.explanation: Plasma is mostly water carrying dissolved food, hormones, salts and wastes.

questions.text: White blood cells mainly help the body to
questions.explanation: Phagocytes engulf germs and lymphocytes make antibodies.

questions.text: Sickle cell anaemia is
options: caused by eating too much sugar
questions.explanation: It is passed from parents to children through genes (genotype SS).

questions.text: Which genotypes, if they marry, could have a child with sickle cell anaemia?
questions.explanation: Two AS carriers each have a 1 in 2 chance of passing S, so 1 in 4 of their children could be SS.

questions.text: Which blood vessel carries blood from the lungs to the heart?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary vein is the only vein that carries oxygenated blood.

questions.text: Which blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary artery is the only artery carrying deoxygenated blood.

questions.text: Valves in veins
questions.explanation: Blood in veins is at low pressure, so valves keep it moving towards the heart.

questions.text: Food made in the leaves is carried to other parts of the plant through the
questions.explanation: The movement of food in the phloem is called translocation.

questions.text: Which muscle contracts and flattens when we breathe in?
questions.explanation: When the diaphragm and intercostal muscles contract, the chest volume increases and air flows in.

questions.text: Which gas is present in a higher percentage in exhaled air than in inhaled air?
questions.explanation: Exhaled air has about 4% carbon dioxide compared with about 0.04% in inhaled air.

questions.text: Fish obtain oxygen from water through their
questions.explanation: Water passes over the gill filaments, where oxygen diffuses into the blood.

questions.text: Which hormone prepares the body for "fight or flight"?
questions.explanation: Adrenaline raises the heart rate and blood sugar in an emergency.

questions.text: Lack of iodine in the diet causes
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed to make thyroxine; lack of it makes the thyroid gland swell.

questions.text: The growth of roots downwards in response to gravity is
questions.explanation: Roots grow towards gravity; shoots grow away from it.

questions.text: The physical appearance of an organism is its
questions.explanation: The genotype is the genetic make-up; the phenotype is what you can see.

questions.text: Different forms of the same gene are called
questions.explanation: For example, the gene for height may have a tall allele and a short allele.

questions.text: How many chromosomes are in a normal human body cell?
questions.explanation: Body cells have 23 pairs (46). Sex cells have 23.

questions.text: Which type of cell division produces sex cells (gametes)?
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number.

questions.text: Which of these is a sexually transmitted infection?
questions.explanation: Gonorrhoea is a bacterial infection passed on through sexual contact.

questions.text: Menstruation is the
options: monthly shedding of the lining of the uterus
questions.explanation: If no fertilisation occurs, the thickened uterine lining breaks down and is shed.

questions.text: Ovulation is the release of
questions.explanation: Ovulation usually happens about the middle of the menstrual cycle.

questions.text: Which method can prevent both pregnancy and the spread of HIV?
questions.explanation: Condoms form a barrier against sperm and many infections.

questions.text: Which hormone maintains the thick lining of the uterus during pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Progesterone keeps the uterine lining ready to support the embryo.

questions.text: Identical twins are formed when
options: one egg is fertilised by two sperms
one fertilised egg splits into two
two eggs are fertilised by two sperms
questions.explanation: Identical twins share the same genes because they come from one zygote.

questions.text: Which of these is a characteristic of all living things?
options: they move from place to place
questions.explanation: All living things respire to release energy. Only green plants photosynthesise.

questions.text: Which kingdom do mushrooms belong to?
questions.explanation: Mushrooms do not photosynthesise and have cell walls made of chitin, so they are fungi.

questions.text: The system of giving every organism a two-part scientific name is called
questions.explanation: Each organism has a genus name and a species name, e.g. Homo sapiens.

questions.text: Which of these animals is a mammal?
questions.explanation: Bats have hair and feed their young with milk, so they are mammals.

questions.text: Which group of organisms has no true nucleus?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes: their genetic material is not enclosed in a nucleus.

questions.text: Which feature is found in insects?
questions.explanation: Insects have three body parts (head, thorax, abdomen) and three pairs of legs.

questions.text: Which organelle is the site of aerobic respiration?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria release energy from food by aerobic respiration.

questions.text: Which structure is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall. Animal cells do not.

questions.text: Which organelle controls the activities of the cell?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains the chromosomes and controls cell activities.

questions.text: Where does protein synthesis take place in a cell?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes join amino acids together to make proteins.

questions.text: Which organelle contains chlorophyll?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts trap light energy for photosynthesis.

questions.text: Who first described cells, after looking at cork under a microscope?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke named "cells" in 1665 after observing cork.

questions.text: The movement of water molecules from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution through a selectively permeable membrane is called
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane.

questions.text: When a plant cell is placed in a concentrated salt solution, it becomes
questions.explanation: Water leaves the cell by osmosis and the cytoplasm shrinks away from the cell wall.

questions.text: The smell of perfume spreading through a room is an example of
questions.explanation: Perfume molecules move from a region of high concentration to low concentration.

questions.text: What happens to a red blood cell placed in distilled water?
questions.explanation: Water enters by osmosis. Animal cells have no cell wall, so the cell bursts (haemolysis).

questions.text: Which process needs energy from the cell to move substances against a concentration gradient?
questions.explanation: Active transport uses energy (ATP) to move substances from low to high concentration.

questions.text: Why does sprinkling salt on a garden snail harm it?
options: water is drawn out of its body by osmosis
the salt gives it too much energy
the snail absorbs too much water
questions.explanation: The salt makes the surface very concentrated, so water leaves the snail's cells.

questions.text: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ in the presence of light and chlorophyll.

questions.text: Which gas is given off during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is released when water is split during the light stage.

questions.text: Which chemical is used to test a leaf for starch?
questions.explanation: Iodine turns blue-black in the presence of starch.

questions.text: Which mineral element is needed to make chlorophyll?
questions.explanation: Magnesium is at the centre of the chlorophyll molecule. Lack of it causes yellowing (chlorosis).

questions.text: The tiny pores on leaves through which gases enter and leave are called
questions.explanation: Stomata, controlled by guard cells, allow gas exchange and water loss.

questions.text: Plants that trap insects to get extra nitrogen are described as
questions.explanation: Insectivorous plants such as the sundew digest insects for nitrogen.

questions.text: In the food chain grass → grasshopper → lizard → hawk, which organism is the producer?
questions.explanation: Producers are green plants that make their own food by photosynthesis.

questions.text: In the food chain grass → grasshopper → lizard → hawk, the lizard is a
questions.explanation: The lizard eats the primary consumer (grasshopper), so it is a secondary consumer.

questions.text: What is the role of decomposers in an ecosystem?
options: they break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil
questions.explanation: Bacteria and fungi recycle nutrients from dead organisms.

questions.text: All the organisms of one species living in an area make up a
questions.explanation: A population is one species in one area. A community includes all species.

questions.text: The relationship between a tapeworm and its human host is
questions.explanation: The tapeworm benefits while the host is harmed.

questions.text: The relationship between nitrogen-fixing bacteria and the roots of beans is
questions.explanation: The bacteria get food and shelter; the plant gets nitrogen compounds. Both benefit.

questions.text: Which joint allows movement in all directions?
questions.explanation: The shoulder and hip are ball-and-socket joints.

questions.text: The elbow is an example of a
questions.explanation: A hinge joint allows movement in one plane only, like a door.

questions.text: Which tissue joins a muscle to a bone?
questions.explanation: Tendons attach muscles to bones. Ligaments join bone to bone.

questions.text: The skeleton of an insect is described as an
questions.explanation: Insects have a hard outer covering made of chitin.

questions.text: Which mineral is important for strong bones and teeth?
questions.explanation: Calcium (with phosphorus) hardens bones and teeth.

questions.text: Which tissue provides support in young plant stems?
questions.explanation: Collenchyma cells have thickened corners that give flexible support.

questions.text: Which enzyme in saliva begins the digestion of starch?
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase breaks starch down to maltose.

questions.text: Where is most digested food absorbed?
questions.explanation: The ileum has villi that give a large surface area for absorption.

questions.text: Which food class is mainly for body building and repair?
questions.explanation: Proteins are made of amino acids that build and repair tissues.

questions.text: A shortage of vitamin C causes
questions.explanation: Scurvy causes bleeding gums. Rickets is caused by lack of vitamin D.

questions.text: What is the role of bile in digestion?
questions.explanation: Bile breaks fats into tiny droplets, giving lipase a larger surface to work on.

questions.text: Kwashiorkor in children is caused by a lack of
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor is a protein-deficiency disease, with a swollen belly and thin limbs.

questions.text: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart under high pressure.

questions.text: Which blood cells help in clotting?
questions.explanation: Platelets release substances that start the clotting process.

questions.text: Which chamber of the heart pumps blood to the whole body?
questions.explanation: The left ventricle has the thickest wall and pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta.

questions.text: Water moves up a plant from the roots to the leaves through the
questions.explanation: Xylem vessels carry water and mineral salts upwards.

questions.text: The loss of water vapour from the leaves of a plant is called
questions.explanation: Water evaporates from leaf cells and escapes through the stomata.

questions.text: Which pigment in red blood cells carries oxygen?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin combines with oxygen to form oxyhaemoglobin.

questions.text: What are the products of aerobic respiration?
questions.explanation: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + energy.

questions.text: During vigorous exercise, muscles respire anaerobically and produce
questions.explanation: Lactic acid builds up and causes muscle fatigue.

questions.text: Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces
questions.explanation: This is fermentation, used in brewing and baking.

questions.text: Gaseous exchange in the human lungs takes place in the
questions.explanation: The alveoli are thin-walled air sacs surrounded by capillaries.

questions.text: In which part of the cell does aerobic respiration mainly take place?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are called the "powerhouse" of the cell.

questions.text: Through which structures do insects breathe?
questions.explanation: Air enters through spiracles and reaches the cells through a network of tracheae.

questions.text: Which organ removes urea from the blood?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter urea from the blood and pass it out in urine.

questions.text: The functional unit of the kidney is the
questions.explanation: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons, which filter blood.

questions.text: Which substance is excreted by the lungs?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide from respiration diffuses out of the blood in the lungs.

questions.text: Where is urea made in the human body?
questions.explanation: The liver breaks down excess amino acids (deamination) and forms urea.

questions.text: Which of these is an excretory product of plants?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is a waste product of photosynthesis, as well as carbon dioxide from respiration.

questions.text: The skin helps in excretion by producing
questions.explanation: Sweat contains water, salts and small amounts of urea.

questions.text: The basic unit of the nervous system is the
questions.explanation: Neurons are nerve cells that carry electrical impulses.

questions.text: Which hormone controls blood sugar level by lowering it?
questions.explanation: Insulin from the pancreas helps cells take up glucose, lowering blood sugar.

questions.text: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination of movement?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates muscle movement and balance.

questions.text: Pulling your hand away quickly from a hot object is an example of a
questions.explanation: A reflex is fast and automatic, passing through the spinal cord.

questions.text: Which gland is often called the "master gland"?
questions.explanation: The pituitary releases hormones that control many other glands.

questions.text: The growth of a plant shoot towards light is called
questions.explanation: Auxins collect on the shaded side and make it grow faster, so the shoot bends to the light.

questions.text: The transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma is called
questions.explanation: Pollination comes before fertilisation.

questions.text: After fertilisation, the ovary develops into the
questions.explanation: The ovary becomes the fruit and the ovules become the seeds.

questions.text: Which part of a flower produces pollen grains?
questions.explanation: The anther is the top part of the stamen.

questions.text: Fruits such as those of the shea tree and mango are mainly dispersed by
questions.explanation: Animals eat the fleshy fruit and drop or pass out the seeds elsewhere.

questions.text: Which method of propagation uses part of a stem to grow a new plant, as in cassava?
questions.explanation: Cassava is propagated by planting stem cuttings.

questions.text: Which condition is NOT needed for a seed to germinate?
questions.explanation: Most seeds need water, oxygen and warmth to germinate. Light is not usually required.

questions.text: Where does fertilisation take place in humans?
questions.explanation: The sperm meets the egg in the oviduct.

questions.text: Which organ produces sperm in human males?
questions.explanation: Sperm are produced in the testes.

questions.text: The structure through which a foetus gets food and oxygen from the mother is the
questions.explanation: Substances pass between mother and foetus across the placenta.

questions.text: The stages in the life cycle of a mosquito are
questions.explanation: Mosquitoes undergo complete metamorphosis.

questions.text: Which hormone is mainly responsible for male secondary sexual characteristics?
questions.explanation: Testosterone causes changes such as deepening of the voice and growth of facial hair.

questions.text: Animals such as birds and reptiles that lay eggs are described as
questions.explanation: Oviparous animals lay eggs that develop outside the mother's body.

questions.text: In a cross between two heterozygous plants (Tt × Tt), what fraction of the offspring is expected to be short (tt)?
questions.explanation: The offspring ratio is 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so 1/4 are tt.

questions.text: Who is known as the father of genetics?
questions.explanation: Mendel worked out the laws of inheritance using garden peas.

questions.text: A man with blood group AB marries a woman with blood group O. Which blood groups can their children have?
questions.explanation: The father passes A or B; the mother passes O. The children are AO (group A) or BO (group B).

questions.text: Which sex chromosomes does a human male have?
questions.explanation: Males have one X and one Y chromosome. Females have two X chromosomes.

questions.text: The basic unit of inheritance is the
questions.explanation: Genes are sections of DNA on chromosomes that carry hereditary information.

questions.text: Which of these is an example of continuous variation?
questions.explanation: Height shows a range of values. The others fall into distinct groups.

questions.text: Who proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.explanation: Darwin published his theory in "On the Origin of Species" in 1859.

questions.text: Lamarck's theory of evolution is based on
options: use and disuse of body parts
questions.explanation: Lamarck believed features developed through use were passed to offspring.

questions.text: Which of these is evidence for evolution?
questions.explanation: Fossils show how organisms have changed over long periods.

questions.text: "Survival of the fittest" means that
options: the strongest animals always win fights
organisms best suited to their environment survive and reproduce
questions.explanation: Organisms with useful variations are more likely to pass on their genes.

questions.text: A sudden change in the genetic material of an organism is called a
questions.explanation: Mutations can create new variations for natural selection to act on.

questions.text: The forelimbs of a human, a bat and a whale have a similar bone structure. These are called
questions.explanation: Homologous structures suggest a common ancestor.

questions.text: Which organism causes malaria?
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by the parasite Plasmodium. The female Anopheles mosquito carries it.

questions.text: Cholera is mainly spread through
questions.explanation: Cholera bacteria spread through water or food contaminated with faeces.

questions.text: Which disease is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: Measles is caused by a virus. TB and typhoid are bacterial; malaria is caused by a protozoan.

questions.text: Vaccination protects people from disease by
options: stimulating the body to produce antibodies
killing all bacteria in the body
questions.explanation: A vaccine trains the immune system to recognise and fight a germ.

questions.text: Which vector transmits river blindness (onchocerciasis)?
questions.explanation: Blackflies breed in fast-flowing rivers and transmit the worm that causes river blindness.

questions.text: Sleeping sickness is transmitted by the
questions.explanation: The tsetse fly carries Trypanosoma, the parasite that causes sleeping sickness.

questions.text: Cacti have spines instead of broad leaves to
questions.explanation: Spines have a small surface area, which reduces transpiration in dry habitats.

questions.text: Which feature helps fish live in water?
questions.explanation: Gills take in dissolved oxygen from water.

questions.text: Mangrove plants have breathing roots (pneumatophores) because
options: the waterlogged mud has little oxygen
questions.explanation: Pneumatophores stick out of the mud to take in air.

questions.text: Which of these is a method of wildlife conservation?
options: creating game reserves and national parks
questions.explanation: Protected areas such as Yankari Game Reserve help conserve wildlife.

questions.text: The gradual change in the types of species in an area over time is called
questions.explanation: For example, bare rock may be colonised by lichens, then mosses, grasses and later shrubs.

questions.text: Why do desert animals such as camels produce very concentrated urine?
questions.explanation: Producing little water in the urine helps them survive where water is scarce.

questions.text: Which apparatus is used to measure a fixed volume of liquid accurately, such as 25.0 cm³, in titration?
questions.explanation: A pipette delivers one exact volume. A burette measures variable volumes.

questions.text: Which apparatus delivers a variable volume of acid during a titration?
questions.explanation: The burette has a tap and is read before and after each titration.

questions.text: What should you do first if a corrosive chemical splashes onto your skin?
options: cover it with a bandage immediately
rub it in with a cloth
wash it off with plenty of running water
ignore it until the practical ends
questions.explanation: Plenty of water dilutes and removes the chemical. Then tell the teacher.

questions.text: The hazard symbol showing a flame means the substance is
questions.explanation: Flammable substances catch fire easily, so keep them away from flames.

questions.text: Which apparatus is used to heat a small amount of solid strongly?
questions.explanation: A crucible can withstand very high temperatures.

questions.text: Why should a test tube be pointed away from people when heating it?
options: it cools the test tube faster
questions.explanation: Liquids can boil suddenly and shoot out of the tube.

questions.text: The change of a liquid into a gas below its boiling point is
questions.explanation: Fast-moving particles escape from the surface of the liquid.

questions.text: The temperature at which a pure solid turns into a liquid is its
questions.explanation: Pure substances have sharp melting points; impurities lower and widen them.

questions.text: Why does a gas spread out to fill its container?
options: its particles move freely and randomly in all directions
its particles are heavier than liquid particles
its particles are fixed in place
questions.explanation: Gas particles have weak attractions and high kinetic energy.

questions.text: Which gas diffuses fastest?
questions.explanation: Graham's law: lighter gases diffuse faster. Hydrogen is the lightest gas.

questions.text: Adding salt to water raises its
questions.explanation: Dissolved impurities raise the boiling point and lower the freezing point.

questions.text: A substance that absorbs moisture from the air but does not dissolve is
questions.explanation: Deliquescent substances absorb so much water that they dissolve; efflorescent ones lose water.

questions.text: Which salt is used as table salt?
questions.explanation: Sodium chloride (NaCl) is common salt.

questions.text: Which method is used to prepare an insoluble salt such as barium sulphate?
questions.explanation: Mixing two solutions forms the insoluble salt as a precipitate, which is filtered off.

questions.text: Which salt is used as a fertiliser?
questions.explanation: Ammonium salts supply nitrogen to plants.

questions.text: Which of these salts is insoluble in water?
questions.explanation: All nitrates and all sodium, potassium and ammonium salts are soluble. Silver chloride is insoluble.

questions.text: Water of crystallisation in hydrated copper(II) sulphate gives it a
questions.explanation: Anhydrous copper(II) sulphate is white and turns blue when water is added.

questions.text: An acid salt contains
questions.explanation: For example, sodium hydrogensulphate, NaHSO₄.

questions.text: Diamond and graphite are
questions.explanation: Allotropes are different structural forms of the same element.

questions.text: Why is graphite used in pencils and as a lubricant?
options: its layers slide over each other
it is the hardest natural substance
questions.explanation: Weak forces between layers let them slide easily.

questions.text: Why is diamond used in cutting tools?
questions.explanation: Each carbon atom is strongly bonded to four others in a rigid network.

questions.text: Which form of carbon conducts electricity?
questions.explanation: Graphite has free (delocalised) electrons between its layers.

questions.text: Activated charcoal is used to
questions.explanation: Its large surface area adsorbs gases and coloured impurities.

questions.text: Which gas is produced when charcoal burns in a limited supply of air?
questions.explanation: Incomplete combustion of carbon forms poisonous carbon monoxide.

questions.text: A solution gives a white precipitate with silver nitrate solution in the presence of dilute nitric acid. Which ion is present?
questions.explanation: Silver chloride is a white precipitate that does not dissolve in dilute nitric acid.

questions.text: Adding barium chloride solution to an acidified solution gives a white precipitate. Which ion is present?
questions.explanation: Barium sulphate is a white insoluble precipitate.

questions.text: Which gas turns damp red litmus paper blue?
questions.explanation: Ammonia is the only common alkaline gas.

questions.text: Which gas burns with a "pop" when tested with a lighted splint?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen burns explosively with oxygen in the air.

questions.text: Which metal ion gives a golden-yellow flame?
questions.explanation: Potassium gives lilac, copper blue-green and calcium brick-red.

questions.text: Adding sodium hydroxide solution gives a blue precipitate. Which ion is present?
questions.explanation: Copper(II) hydroxide is blue. Iron(II) gives green and iron(III) gives reddish-brown.

questions.text: Crude oil is mainly a mixture of
questions.explanation: Crude oil contains many alkanes and other hydrocarbons.

questions.text: Breaking long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter, more useful ones is called
questions.explanation: Cracking produces petrol and alkenes from heavy fractions.

questions.text: The octane rating of petrol measures its
questions.explanation: Higher octane petrol burns smoothly without knocking.

questions.text: Which fraction of crude oil is used as aviation fuel and in lanterns?
questions.explanation: Kerosene is used in lamps, stoves and jet engines.

questions.text: Bitumen from crude oil is used for
questions.explanation: Bitumen is the thick residue used to tar roads and waterproof roofs.

questions.text: Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) used for cooking is mainly
questions.explanation: Propane and butane are easily liquefied under pressure.

questions.text: Small molecules that join to form a polymer are called
questions.explanation: For example, ethene monomers join to make polyethene.

questions.text: Polyethene is made by
questions.explanation: Ethene molecules join through their double bonds without losing any small molecule.

questions.text: Which of these is a natural polymer?
questions.explanation: Starch, proteins, cellulose and natural rubber are natural polymers.

questions.text: Proteins are polymers of
questions.explanation: Amino acids are joined by peptide bonds.

questions.text: Which polymer is used to make water pipes?
questions.explanation: Polyvinyl chloride is tough and resistant to water.

questions.text: Thermosetting plastics differ from thermoplastics because they
options: cannot be softened again by heating
questions.explanation: Thermosets set permanently; thermoplastics can be reheated and reshaped.

questions.text: Which raw material is used to make cement?
questions.explanation: Cement is made by heating limestone with clay.

questions.text: Glass is made mainly from
questions.explanation: These are heated together until they melt.

questions.text: Which industry uses the Solvay process?
questions.explanation: The Solvay process makes sodium carbonate from brine, limestone and ammonia.

questions.text: Which is an advantage of locating a chemical industry near its raw materials?
questions.explanation: Bulky raw materials are expensive to move.

questions.text: Which by-product of the Haber process is recycled?
questions.explanation: The yield is only partial, so unreacted gases are passed over the catalyst again.

questions.text: Detergents differ from soap because detergents
questions.explanation: Detergents do not form scum with calcium and magnesium ions.

questions.text: Which force holds molecules of water to each other and gives water its high boiling point?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonds between molecules need extra energy to break.

questions.text: Which compound is formed by covalent bonding?
questions.explanation: Carbon and hydrogen share electrons in CH₄.

questions.text: How many electrons are shared in a double covalent bond?
questions.explanation: A double bond is two shared pairs, as in O₂ and C=C.

questions.text: Which group 1 metal reacts most vigorously with water?
questions.explanation: Reactivity of the alkali metals increases down the group.

questions.text: Which halogen is the most reactive?
questions.explanation: Reactivity of the halogens decreases down the group.

questions.text: Elements that have properties of both metals and non-metals are called
questions.explanation: Silicon and germanium are metalloids.

questions.text: Which of these is a base that dissolves in water (an alkali)?
questions.explanation: An alkali is a soluble base. Most metal oxides are insoluble.

questions.text: Which indicator is pink in alkaline solution and colourless in acid?
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is used in titrations of weak acids with strong bases.

questions.text: A solution with pH 2 is
questions.explanation: The lower the pH below 7, the more acidic the solution.

questions.text: In the reaction Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu, zinc acts as the
questions.explanation: Zinc gives electrons to copper ions, so it is oxidised and acts as the reducing agent.

questions.text: What is the oxidation number of chlorine in NaCl?
questions.explanation: Sodium is +1, so chlorine must be −1 for the compound to be neutral.

questions.text: What is the oxidation number of any element in its free (uncombined) state?
questions.explanation: For example, O₂, Fe and Cl₂ all have an oxidation number of 0.

questions.text: Which method is best for separating sand from water?
questions.explanation: Sand is insoluble, so it stays on the filter paper while water passes through.

questions.text: Which method is best for obtaining pure water from salt water?
questions.explanation: Distillation boils off the water and condenses it, leaving the salt behind.

questions.text: Which method separates the different dyes in black ink?
questions.explanation: The dyes travel different distances on the paper, so they separate into bands.

questions.text: Which method separates a mixture of iodine and sand?
questions.explanation: Iodine sublimes on heating and can be collected on a cold surface, leaving the sand.

questions.text: Petrol, kerosene and diesel are separated from crude oil by
questions.explanation: The fractions have different boiling ranges, so they condense at different heights in the column.

questions.text: Which method separates two liquids that do not mix, such as oil and water?
questions.explanation: Immiscible liquids form layers, and the lower layer is run off through the tap of a separating funnel.

questions.text: Which of these is an element?
questions.explanation: An element contains only one kind of atom. Water and salt are compounds; air is a mixture.

questions.text: Which of these is a mixture?
questions.explanation: Air is a mixture of nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide and other gases in no fixed ratio.

questions.text: Which is a property of a compound?
options: its elements are combined in a fixed ratio
it has no definite melting point
its parts can be separated by physical means
its properties are the average of its parts
questions.explanation: A compound has a fixed composition and can only be separated by chemical means.

questions.text: Which of these is a physical change?
questions.explanation: Melting changes only the state; no new substance is formed and it can be reversed.

questions.text: Which of these is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Burning forms new substances (carbon dioxide and water) and cannot easily be reversed.

questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
questions.explanation: Sodium's symbol comes from its Latin name, natrium.

questions.text: An atom has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. What is its mass number?
questions.explanation: Mass number = protons + neutrons = 11 + 12 = 23.

questions.text: Which particle has a negative charge?
questions.explanation: Electrons are negative, protons are positive and neutrons have no charge.

questions.text: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons are called
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers, e.g. carbon-12 and carbon-14.

questions.text: What is the electron configuration of an atom with atomic number 12?
questions.explanation: The first shell holds 2 electrons and the second holds 8, leaving 2 in the third shell.

questions.text: Chlorine has an atomic number of 17. How many electrons are in its outermost shell?
questions.explanation: 2, 8, 7: there are 7 electrons in the outer shell.

questions.text: Who proposed that electrons move round the nucleus in fixed energy levels?
questions.explanation: Bohr's model placed electrons in definite shells (energy levels).

questions.text: Elements in the same group of the periodic table have the same
questions.explanation: Elements in a group have the same number of valence electrons, so they react in similar ways.

questions.text: Which group contains the noble gases?
questions.explanation: The noble gases have full outer shells and are very unreactive.

questions.text: The alkali metals are found in
questions.explanation: Lithium, sodium and potassium are Group 1 alkali metals with one outer electron.

questions.text: Which element is a halogen?
questions.explanation: The halogens (Group 7) include fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine.

questions.text: Across a period from left to right, the atomic radius generally
questions.explanation: The increasing nuclear charge pulls the electrons closer, so atoms get smaller across a period.

questions.text: An element has the electron configuration 2, 8, 3. In which period is it?
questions.explanation: The period number equals the number of occupied shells. Three shells means Period 3.

questions.text: Which type of bond holds the atoms in a water molecule together?
questions.explanation: Oxygen and hydrogen share electron pairs, which is covalent bonding.

questions.text: Which type of bond is formed between sodium and chlorine in sodium chloride?
questions.explanation: Sodium gives an electron to chlorine, forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions held by electrostatic attraction.

questions.text: Ionic compounds usually
options: do not conduct electricity when molten
questions.explanation: Strong attraction between ions gives ionic compounds high melting points.

questions.text: How many covalent bonds does carbon usually form?
questions.explanation: Carbon has 4 outer electrons and shares all four, for example in methane (CH₄).

questions.text: Metals conduct electricity because they have
options: shared electron pairs between two atoms
questions.explanation: In metallic bonding, the outer electrons are free to move through the metal.

questions.text: In which compound is there a dative (coordinate) bond?
questions.explanation: In NH₄⁺, nitrogen donates both electrons of its lone pair to H⁺.

questions.text: What is the chemical formula of calcium carbonate?
questions.explanation: Calcium (Ca²⁺) combines with carbonate (CO₃²⁻) in a 1:1 ratio.

questions.text: What is the valency of oxygen in most of its compounds?
questions.explanation: Oxygen gains 2 electrons to complete its outer shell, so its valency is 2.

questions.text: Balance the equation: H₂ + O₂ → H₂O. What number goes in front of H₂O?
questions.explanation: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O has 4 hydrogen atoms and 2 oxygen atoms on each side.

questions.text: What is the formula of aluminium oxide?
questions.explanation: Al³⁺ and O²⁻ combine as 2 × 3 = 3 × 2, giving Al₂O₃.

questions.text: What does (aq) mean after a formula in an equation?
questions.explanation: (aq) means aqueous: the substance is in solution in water.

questions.text: What is the name of the compound with the formula H₂SO₄?
questions.explanation: H₂SO₄ is sulphuric(VI) acid. Sulphurous acid is H₂SO₃.

questions.text: What is the relative molecular mass of CO₂? (C = 12, O = 16)
How many moles are in 36 g of water? (H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Molar mass of H₂O = 18 g/mol. Moles = 36 ÷ 18 = 2.

questions.text: What is the molar volume of any gas at s.t.p.?
questions.explanation: One mole of any gas occupies 22.4 dm³ at standard temperature and pressure.

questions.text: How many particles are in one mole of a substance?
questions.explanation: This is the Avogadro constant.

questions.text: What mass of sodium hydroxide is needed to make 1 dm³ of a 0.5 mol/dm³ solution? (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
questions.explanation: Molar mass of NaOH = 40 g/mol. Mass = 0.5 × 40 = 20 g.

questions.text: What is the empirical formula of a compound whose molecular formula is C₆H₁₂O₆?
questions.explanation: Divide all subscripts by 6 to get the simplest ratio: CH₂O.

questions.text: What is the pH of a neutral solution at 25 °C?
questions.explanation: pH 7 is neutral. Below 7 is acidic and above 7 is alkaline.

questions.text: What colour does blue litmus paper turn in an acid?
questions.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red.

questions.text: What are the products when an acid reacts with a base?
questions.explanation: This is neutralisation: acid + base → salt + water.

questions.text: What gas is produced when zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂.

questions.text: Which of these is a strong acid?
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid ionises completely in water. The others ionise only partly.

questions.text: What gas is given off when an acid reacts with a carbonate?
questions.explanation: Acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide.

questions.text: Oxidation is defined as
questions.explanation: Remember OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain (of electrons).

questions.text: What is the oxidation number of manganese in KMnO₄?
questions.explanation: K = +1 and 4 O = −8, so Mn + 1 − 8 = 0, giving Mn = +7.

questions.text: In the reaction CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, which substance is reduced?
questions.explanation: CuO loses oxygen to become Cu, so it is reduced.

questions.text: A substance that accepts electrons is called
questions.explanation: An oxidising agent gains (accepts) electrons and is itself reduced.

questions.text: What is the oxidation number of sulphur in H₂SO₄?
Rusting of iron is an example of
questions.explanation: Iron combines with oxygen (in the presence of water) and loses electrons.

questions.text: In electrolysis, the positive electrode is called the
questions.explanation: The anode is positive and attracts negative ions (anions).

questions.text: During the electrolysis of acidified water, what gas is given off at the cathode?
questions.explanation: Positive H⁺ ions move to the cathode and gain electrons to form hydrogen gas.

questions.text: Which of these can act as an electrolyte?
questions.explanation: An electrolyte must contain ions free to move, as in a molten or dissolved ionic compound.

questions.text: Electroplating a spoon with silver: the spoon should be made the
questions.explanation: Silver ions are deposited as silver metal at the cathode, so the spoon is the cathode.

questions.text: During the electrolysis of brine, what gas is produced at the anode?
questions.explanation: Chloride ions are discharged at the anode as chlorine gas.

questions.text: What is the name of the law that relates the mass deposited in electrolysis to the quantity of electricity?
questions.explanation: Faraday's first law: the mass of substance deposited is proportional to the quantity of electricity passed.

questions.text: Which change will increase the rate of reaction between marble chips and acid?
options: using powdered marble instead of chips
questions.explanation: Powder has a larger surface area, so more particles can collide at once.

questions.text: A catalyst speeds up a reaction by
options: increasing the amount of product at equilibrium
being used up in the reaction
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides another pathway with lower activation energy and is not used up.

questions.text: Why does increasing temperature increase the rate of reaction?
