options: particles move faster and collide more often with enough energy
questions.explanation: More particles have energy equal to or greater than the activation energy.

questions.text: For the equilibrium N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, increasing the pressure will
options: shift the equilibrium to the left
shift the equilibrium to the right
questions.explanation: By Le Chatelier's principle, the equilibrium shifts towards fewer gas molecules (4 on the left, 2 on the right).

questions.text: An exothermic reaction is one that
options: takes in heat from the surroundings
gives out heat to the surroundings
questions.explanation: Exothermic reactions release heat, so the surroundings get warmer. ΔH is negative.

questions.text: Which of these is an endothermic process?
options: neutralising an acid with a base
questions.explanation: Ammonium chloride absorbs heat as it dissolves, so the solution feels cold.

questions.text: What causes temporary hardness of water?
questions.explanation: Calcium (or magnesium) hydrogencarbonate causes temporary hardness, which boiling removes.

questions.text: Temporary hardness can be removed by
questions.explanation: Boiling decomposes the hydrogencarbonate into insoluble calcium carbonate.

questions.text: A solution that cannot dissolve any more solute at a given temperature is
questions.explanation: A saturated solution holds the maximum amount of solute at that temperature.

questions.text: Which substance is added to water in treatment plants to kill germs?
questions.explanation: Chlorine is a disinfectant that kills bacteria in water.

questions.text: Hard water does not lather easily with soap because
options: calcium and magnesium ions form scum with soap
questions.explanation: The ions react with soap to form an insoluble scum instead of lather.

questions.text: Why is alum (potash alum) added during water treatment?
options: to make suspended particles clump together and settle
questions.explanation: Alum causes coagulation, so fine particles settle and can be removed.

questions.text: What is the general formula of the alkanes?
questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

questions.text: Which compound decolourises bromine water quickly?
questions.explanation: Ethene has a C=C double bond and undergoes addition with bromine. Alkanes do not.

questions.text: What is the name of CH₃CH₂CH₃?
questions.explanation: Three carbon atoms with only single bonds make propane.

questions.text: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures are called
questions.explanation: For example, butane and 2-methylpropane are both C₄H₁₀.

questions.text: The main constituent of natural gas is
questions.explanation: Natural gas is mostly methane (CH₄).

questions.text: Ethyne (C₂H₂) is used in oxy-acetylene flames for
questions.explanation: Burning ethyne in oxygen gives a very hot flame used in welding.

questions.text: What is the functional group of alcohols?
questions.explanation: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl group, as in ethanol, C₂H₅OH.

questions.text: The production of ethanol from sugar using yeast is called
questions.explanation: Yeast enzymes convert sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.text: An alcohol reacts with a carboxylic acid to form
questions.explanation: This is esterification. Esters often have fruity smells.

questions.text: Soap is made by heating fats or oils with
questions.explanation: This process is called saponification.

questions.text: What is the functional group of carboxylic acids?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids such as ethanoic acid (vinegar) contain the −COOH group.

questions.text: Which compound is the main acid in vinegar?
questions.explanation: Vinegar is a dilute solution of ethanoic (acetic) acid.

questions.text: Which metal is extracted from bauxite?
questions.explanation: Bauxite is the main ore of aluminium, which is extracted by electrolysis.

questions.text: Iron is extracted in the blast furnace by reduction with
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide reduces iron(III) oxide to iron.

questions.text: Which metal is the most reactive?
questions.explanation: Potassium is near the top of the reactivity series.

questions.text: Galvanising protects iron from rusting by coating it with
questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive, so it corrodes in place of the iron (sacrificial protection).

questions.text: An alloy of copper and zinc is called
questions.explanation: Brass is copper and zinc. Bronze is copper and tin.

questions.text: Which ore of tin is mined in Jos, Plateau State?
questions.explanation: Cassiterite (tin oxide) has long been mined on the Jos Plateau.

questions.text: Which gas makes up about 78% of the air?
questions.explanation: Air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.

questions.text: Ammonia is manufactured industrially by the
questions.explanation: In the Haber process nitrogen and hydrogen combine over an iron catalyst.

questions.text: Sulphuric acid is manufactured by the
questions.explanation: The Contact process oxidises SO₂ to SO₃ over a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst.

questions.text: Which test confirms carbon dioxide?
questions.explanation: CO₂ reacts with limewater (calcium hydroxide) to form a white precipitate of calcium carbonate.

questions.text: Which gas relights a glowing splint?
questions.explanation: Oxygen supports combustion, so a glowing splint bursts into flame.

questions.text: Which gas bleaches damp litmus paper?
questions.explanation: Chlorine forms an acid with water that bleaches the dye.

questions.text: Which gas is the main cause of acid rain?
questions.explanation: Sulphur dioxide dissolves in rain water to form acids.

questions.text: Which gas is the main contributor to the greenhouse effect?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide traps heat radiated from the earth's surface.

questions.text: Carbon monoxide is dangerous because it
options: combines with haemoglobin and stops it carrying oxygen
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide binds strongly to haemoglobin, reducing oxygen transport in the blood.

questions.text: Gas flaring in the Niger Delta mainly releases
options: carbon dioxide and other pollutants into the air
questions.explanation: Burning off gas releases carbon dioxide, soot and other pollutants.

questions.text: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are harmful because they
questions.explanation: CFCs break down ozone, which shields the earth from ultraviolet rays.

questions.text: Which of these materials is biodegradable?
questions.explanation: Paper can be broken down by microorganisms. Most plastics cannot.

questions.text: A warehouse is mainly used to
options: store goods until they are needed
questions.explanation: Warehousing bridges the gap between production and consumption.

questions.text: A warehouse where imported goods are kept until customs duty is paid is a
questions.explanation: Duty is paid only when the goods are released.

questions.text: Which type of warehouse is best for storing fish and meat?
questions.explanation: Low temperatures keep perishable goods fresh.

questions.text: Warehousing helps to stabilise prices by
options: releasing goods when supply is low
questions.explanation: Stored goods can be sold during scarcity.

questions.text: Tourism contributes to an economy by
options: earning foreign exchange and creating jobs
questions.explanation: Visitors spend money on hotels, transport and attractions.

questions.text: Which body promotes tourism in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: It promotes and regulates tourism.

questions.text: The stock exchange is a market for
options: buying and selling shares and bonds
questions.explanation: In Nigeria it is called the Nigerian Exchange (NGX).

questions.text: A person who buys and sells shares on behalf of clients is a
questions.explanation: Stockbrokers are licensed dealers on the exchange.

questions.text: A speculator who buys shares expecting their prices to rise is called a
questions.explanation: A bear expects prices to fall; a stag buys new issues to sell quickly.

questions.text: A speculator who sells shares expecting prices to fall is a
questions.explanation: The bear hopes to buy back later at a lower price.

questions.text: The body that regulates the capital market in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The SEC protects investors and supervises the market.

questions.text: A government bond is a
options: loan to the government that pays interest
questions.explanation: Bonds are long-term debt securities.

questions.text: Buying goods now and paying later is called buying on
questions.explanation: Credit allows consumers to enjoy goods before paying for them.

questions.text: Under a credit sale, ownership of the goods passes to the buyer
questions.explanation: Unlike hire purchase, ownership passes at once.

questions.text: Which body sets standards for products made or sold in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: SON checks that products meet quality standards.

questions.text: The body that regulates food and drugs in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: NAFDAC registers and controls food, drugs and cosmetics.

questions.text: Which is a right of consumers?
options: the right to avoid all taxes
questions.explanation: Consumers are entitled to safety, information and redress.

questions.text: A disadvantage of buying on credit is that
options: the buyer may get into debt
questions.explanation: Easy credit can lead people to overspend.

questions.text: An entrepreneur is a person who
options: only buys goods for personal use
organises resources and takes risks to start a business
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs combine land, labour and capital to produce goods or services.

questions.text: Which is a common source of capital for a small business?
options: the stock exchange for small traders
questions.explanation: Many small businesses start with savings, family loans or cooperatives.

questions.text: A business plan is important because it
options: is required by law for all hawkers
sets out the goals, costs and strategy of a business
questions.explanation: A plan helps the owner and lenders understand the business.

questions.text: Which of these is an entrepreneurial skill?
questions.explanation: Successful entrepreneurs spot opportunities and take calculated risks.

questions.text: "Ajo" or "esusu" is an example of
questions.explanation: Members contribute regularly and each takes the pot in turn.

questions.text: Which body supports small and medium enterprises in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria helps small businesses.

questions.text: A chain of shops owned by one company selling the same goods is called a
questions.explanation: Chain stores benefit from bulk buying.

questions.text: Which retailer usually offers personal service and credit to regular customers?
questions.explanation: Small shopkeepers know their customers personally.

questions.text: A trader who sells goods on behalf of another for a commission is a
questions.explanation: The agent does not own the goods.

questions.text: The bank to which a cheque is addressed is the
questions.explanation: The drawee bank pays the payee.

questions.text: Which banking service allows customers to withdraw cash at any time using a card?
questions.explanation: ATMs give access to cash outside banking hours.

questions.text: Microfinance banks mainly serve
questions.explanation: They give small loans and savings services.

questions.text: The principle that a person must stand to lose financially from the loss of what is insured is
questions.explanation: You cannot insure your neighbour's car for your own benefit.

questions.text: After paying a claim, the insurer takes over the insured's rights against a third party. This is
questions.explanation: The insurer can then recover the loss from whoever caused it.

questions.text: Life assurance differs from insurance because it covers
options: an event that is certain to happen, such as death
questions.explanation: Assurance covers certain events; insurance covers possible risks.

questions.text: Commerce is best defined as
options: all activities involved in the distribution of goods and services
the production of goods in factories
questions.explanation: Commerce covers trade and the aids to trade that get goods to consumers.

questions.text: Which of these is an aid to trade?
questions.explanation: Aids to trade include banking, insurance, transport, communication, warehousing and advertising.

questions.text: Trade between people within the same country is
questions.explanation: Home trade includes both retail and wholesale trade within a country.

questions.text: The exchange of goods for goods without using money is
questions.explanation: Barter needs a double coincidence of wants.

questions.text: Which of these is a direct service?
options: the work of a factory worker
questions.explanation: Direct services are given personally to people, e.g. doctors, lawyers and teachers.

questions.text: Which occupation is found in the industrial sector?
questions.explanation: Industry covers extraction, manufacturing and construction.

questions.text: A retailer is a trader who
options: buys directly from manufacturers in very large quantities
sells goods in small quantities to final consumers
questions.explanation: The retailer is the last link in the chain of distribution.

questions.text: Which of these is a function of the wholesaler?
questions.explanation: The wholesaler buys in bulk from producers and sells in smaller lots to retailers.

questions.text: A large shop with many departments under one roof is a
questions.explanation: Department stores sell many kinds of goods in separate departments.

questions.text: Self-service shops that sell mainly food and household goods are called
questions.explanation: Customers pick their own goods and pay at the checkout.

questions.text: Hawkers are retailers who
options: move from place to place selling goods
questions.explanation: Hawkers carry their goods around, often on their heads or in wheelbarrows.

questions.text: The chain of distribution normally runs from
options: consumer to retailer to wholesaler to producer
producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer
questions.explanation: Goods move from producers through middlemen to consumers.

questions.text: Selling goods to other countries is
questions.explanation: Exports earn foreign exchange.

questions.text: Importing goods to re-export them to other countries is
questions.explanation: Entrepôt (re-export) trade is common in ports such as Singapore.

questions.text: The document an importer sends to an overseas supplier to order goods is an
questions.explanation: An indent is an order for goods from abroad.

questions.text: A bill of lading is a document used in
questions.explanation: It is a receipt for goods shipped and a document of title.

questions.text: The government agency that collects import duties in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The Customs Service collects duties and controls imports and exports.

questions.text: A limit placed on the quantity of a good that can be imported is a
questions.explanation: Quotas restrict the volume of imports.

questions.text: A document from a seller to a buyer giving details of goods sold and the amount due is an
questions.explanation: The invoice tells the buyer how much to pay.

questions.text: A document sent to a customer to correct an overcharge on an invoice is a
questions.explanation: A credit note reduces the amount the buyer owes.

questions.text: A document sent by a buyer to ask about prices and terms is an
questions.explanation: An enquiry starts the buying process.

questions.text: A summary of transactions between a seller and a buyer over a period is a
questions.explanation: It shows the balance the buyer owes at the end of the period.

questions.text: A document given as proof that payment has been made is a
questions.explanation: A receipt confirms payment.

questions.text: A reduction in price given for buying in large quantities is a
questions.explanation: Cash discount is given for prompt payment; trade discount for bulk buying or to traders.

questions.text: A cheque that can only be paid into a bank account is a
questions.explanation: Two parallel lines across a cheque mean it must be paid into an account.

questions.text: A cheque presented more than six months after its date is called
questions.explanation: Banks will not pay a stale cheque.

questions.text: The person who writes and signs a cheque is the
questions.explanation: The drawer orders the bank (drawee) to pay the payee.

questions.text: Which payment method allows money to be sent instantly through a mobile phone or internet banking?
questions.explanation: Electronic transfers move money between accounts almost immediately.

questions.text: Allowing a current account holder to withdraw more than the balance in the account is
questions.explanation: An overdraft is a short-term loan on a current account.

questions.text: An instruction to a bank to make regular fixed payments on a customer's behalf is a
questions.explanation: Standing orders are used for regular payments such as subscriptions.

questions.text: The principle that the insured must disclose all relevant facts is
questions.explanation: Hiding important facts can make the insurance policy void.

questions.text: The principle that the insured should be restored to the same position as before the loss is
questions.explanation: Indemnity prevents the insured from making a profit from a loss.

questions.text: Which type of insurance is compulsory for all vehicle owners in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Third-party insurance covers injury or damage to other people.

questions.text: The amount paid regularly by the insured to the insurer is the
questions.explanation: The premium is the price of insurance cover.

questions.text: Insurance covering ships and their cargo is
questions.explanation: Marine insurance covers risks at sea.

questions.text: Which risk is NOT insurable?
options: loss due to poor business decisions
questions.explanation: Insurers cover risks that can be calculated, not losses from ordinary business decisions.

questions.text: Which mode of transport is fastest over long distances?
questions.explanation: Air transport is fastest but expensive.

questions.text: Pipelines are mostly used to transport
options: liquids and gases such as oil and gas
questions.explanation: Pipelines carry oil, gas and water continuously.

questions.text: Which mode of transport offers door-to-door service?
questions.explanation: Road vehicles can deliver goods directly to the buyer's door.

questions.text: Which body manages Nigeria's seaports?
questions.explanation: The NPA manages port operations.

questions.text: Which means of communication delivers letters and parcels?
questions.explanation: Postal and courier services deliver physical mail and parcels.

questions.text: The main advantage of the internet in commerce is that it
options: allows buying and selling at any time from anywhere
questions.explanation: E-commerce lets customers shop and pay online at any time.

questions.text: Advertising aimed at persuading consumers to buy a particular brand is

its average cost falls as it grows larger

questions.text: Unemployment while workers move between jobs is

questions.text: Diversification of the economy means
options: developing other sectors such as agriculture and manufacturing
questions.explanation: Diversification reduces dependence on a single source of income.

questions.explanation: Line graphs show trends over time clearly.

questions.text: The middle value of data arranged in order is the

questions.text: A balance of payments deficit can be corrected by

questions.text: Foreign exchange reserves are held mainly by the

questions.text: Deflation is

questions.text: Cost-push inflation is caused by

questions.explanation: Legal protection can keep competitors out.

questions.text: Price discrimination means

questions.explanation: For example, lower student prices for the same service.

questions.text: Which international body regulates world trade rules?
questions.explanation: The WTO deals with the rules of trade between nations.

questions.text: Specialisation in international trade is based mainly on

questions.text: The basic economic problem arises because
options: human wants are unlimited while resources are scarce
questions.explanation: Scarcity of resources relative to wants forces people to make choices.

questions.text: Opportunity cost is
options: the total cost of all wants
the next best alternative given up
the money price of a good
questions.explanation: If you buy a textbook instead of shoes, the shoes are the opportunity cost.

questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the alternative forgone, which is the slippers.

questions.text: Arranging wants in order of importance is called a

questions.text: Which of these is a free good?
questions.explanation: Air is not scarce and has no price, so it is a free good.

questions.text: A production possibility curve shows
options: the combinations of two goods an economy can produce with its resources
the prices of goods over time
questions.explanation: Points on the curve show efficient use of all available resources.

questions.text: The law of demand states that, other things being equal,
options: price has no effect on demand
the higher the price, the lower the quantity demanded
the higher the price, the higher the quantity demanded
questions.explanation: Price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions.

questions.text: A demand curve normally slopes
questions.explanation: As price falls, more is demanded, giving a downward slope.

questions.text: An increase in consumers' income will usually cause the demand curve for a normal good to
questions.explanation: Higher income increases demand at every price for normal goods.

questions.text: Tea and coffee are examples of
questions.explanation: Substitutes can be used in place of each other.

questions.text: A movement along a demand curve is caused by a change in
options: the price of the good itself
questions.explanation: Only a change in the good's own price causes a movement along the curve.

questions.text: The law of supply states that, other things being equal,
options: the higher the price, the higher the quantity supplied
the higher the price, the lower the quantity supplied
questions.explanation: Producers offer more for sale when prices are higher.

questions.text: The price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied is the

questions.text: A minimum price set above the equilibrium price leads to
questions.explanation: Producers supply more and consumers buy less, so there is excess supply.

questions.text: A good harvest of tomatoes will most likely cause
options: a rise in the price of tomatoes
a fall in the price of tomatoes
questions.explanation: Supply increases, the supply curve shifts right and price falls.

questions.text: Which of these will shift the supply curve of a good to the left?
options: an increase in the cost of production
a fall in the price of raw materials
questions.explanation: Higher costs mean producers supply less at each price.

questions.text: Which of these are the factors of production?
questions.explanation: These four factors are combined to produce goods and services.

questions.text: The reward for land is
questions.explanation: Land earns rent, labour earns wages, capital earns interest and the entrepreneur earns profit.

questions.text: The reward for the entrepreneur is
questions.explanation: The entrepreneur takes risks and earns profit (or bears losses).

questions.text: Division of labour means
options: breaking production into stages, each done by different workers
questions.explanation: Specialisation in one stage increases speed and skill.

questions.text: Which of these is an example of primary production?
questions.explanation: Primary production takes resources directly from nature: farming, fishing, mining.

questions.text: Which of these is a service (tertiary) occupation?
questions.explanation: Tertiary production provides services rather than goods.

questions.text: A business owned and controlled by one person is called a
questions.explanation: The sole proprietor provides the capital and takes all the profit and risk.

questions.text: The liability of shareholders in a limited liability company is
options: limited to the amount of their shares
questions.explanation: Shareholders can only lose the money they invested.

questions.text: The maximum number of partners in an ordinary partnership is usually
questions.explanation: An ordinary partnership has 2 to 20 partners.

questions.text: A business owned and run by government is a
questions.explanation: Public corporations are set up by law and financed by the government.

questions.text: Which business organisation is based on "one member, one vote"?
questions.explanation: In a cooperative, each member has one vote regardless of shares held.

questions.text: Shares of a public limited company can be bought and sold on the
questions.explanation: Public company shares are traded on the stock exchange.

questions.explanation: Underpopulation means there are too few people to exploit the resources fully.

questions.text: Who are the dependent population?
options: people too young or too old to work
questions.explanation: Children and the elderly depend on the working population.

questions.text: Who put forward the theory that population grows faster than food supply?

questions.text: The movement of workers from one job or place to another is called
questions.explanation: Labour can be geographically or occupationally mobile.

questions.text: A census is
options: an official count of the population
questions.explanation: A census gives data on population size, age, sex and distribution.

questions.text: When the price of a good rises by 10% and quantity demanded falls by 20%, demand is

questions.text: Demand for salt is likely to be

questions.text: If price elasticity of demand is exactly 1, demand is

questions.text: Which of these makes demand for a good more elastic?
options: the good takes a tiny part of income
the good has many close substitutes

questions.text: A vertical demand curve shows demand that is
questions.explanation: Quantity demanded does not change at all when price changes.

questions.text: A market dominated by a few large sellers is

questions.text: Which is a feature of perfect competition?

questions.text: A market with only one buyer is called

questions.text: Monopolistic competition is characterised by

questions.explanation: Excess demand pulls prices up.

questions.text: Which is a function of commercial banks?

questions.text: Per capita income is
questions.explanation: It shows average income per person.

questions.explanation: The income approach sums wages, rent, interest and profit.

questions.text: Net National Product is GNP minus

options: many activities are not recorded, such as subsistence farming

questions.text: A tax whose rate rises as income rises is a

questions.explanation: Indirect taxes are paid on goods and services, not directly on income.

questions.text: When government expenditure is greater than revenue, the budget is in

questions.text: The incidence of a tax refers to
options: who finally bears the burden of the tax
questions.explanation: A tax on a seller may be passed on to buyers through higher prices.

questions.text: Which is a canon (principle) of taxation?
questions.explanation: Adam Smith's canons include certainty, convenience, economy and equality.

questions.text: Devaluation of the naira makes Nigerian exports

questions.text: Terms of trade measure
options: the ratio of export prices to import prices

questions.text: ECOWAS was established in

questions.text: Nigeria is a member of OPEC because it is a major

options: improvements in living standards and welfare

questions.text: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) mainly helps countries with
questions.explanation: The IMF provides short-term support to stabilise countries' external payments.

questions.text: Which sector currently earns Nigeria most of its foreign exchange?
questions.explanation: Petroleum exports have dominated Nigeria's foreign exchange earnings since the 1970s.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "frugal" in this sentence: My uncle lives a frugal life.
questions.explanation: A frugal person is careful not to waste money.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "candid" in this sentence: Thank you for your candid advice.
questions.explanation: Candid advice is honest and direct.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "hostile" in this sentence: The crowd was hostile to the visitors.
questions.explanation: "Hostile" means showing opposition or dislike.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "eminent" in this sentence: An eminent surgeon visited our school.
questions.explanation: An eminent person is famous and respected.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "meagre" in this sentence: He survives on a meagre salary.
questions.explanation: "Meagre" means too small in amount.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "imminent" in this sentence: The storm is imminent.
questions.explanation: "Imminent" means likely to happen very soon. Do not confuse it with "eminent".

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "rectify" in this sentence: Please rectify the error in your work.
questions.explanation: To rectify is to put right.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "ponder" in this sentence: She pondered the question for a while.
questions.explanation: To ponder is to think about something carefully.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "optimistic" in this sentence: Bisi is optimistic about the result.
questions.explanation: An optimist expects good outcomes; a pessimist expects bad ones.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "expand" in this sentence: The company plans to expand.
questions.explanation: To expand is to grow larger; to contract is to become smaller.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "visible" in this sentence: The mountain was visible from the road.
questions.explanation: "Visible" means able to be seen.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "courageous" in this sentence: The courageous soldier saved his friend.
questions.explanation: A courageous person is brave; a cowardly person lacks courage.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "inferior" in this sentence: This cloth is of inferior quality.
questions.explanation: "Inferior" means lower in quality; "superior" means higher.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "accept" in this sentence: She accepted the gift.
questions.explanation: To reject is to refuse to accept.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "punctual" in this sentence: Femi is always punctual.
questions.explanation: A punctual person arrives on time.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "ascend" in this sentence: The climbers ascended the hill.
questions.explanation: To ascend is to go up; to descend is to go down.

questions.text: What does "to bury the hatchet" mean?
options: to make peace after a quarrel
questions.explanation: The idiom means to end a disagreement.

questions.text: What does "to turn over a new leaf" mean?
options: to change one's behaviour for the better
questions.explanation: It means to start behaving better.

questions.text: What does "to beat about the bush" mean?
questions.explanation: Someone who beats about the bush does not get to the point.

questions.text: What does "a wet blanket" refer to?
options: a blanket left in the rain
a person who spoils other people's fun
questions.explanation: A wet blanket discourages others from enjoying themselves.

questions.text: What does "at the eleventh hour" mean?
options: in the middle of the day
questions.explanation: Something done at the eleventh hour is done just in time.

questions.text: What does "to have cold feet" mean?
options: to become nervous and want to back out
questions.explanation: Someone with cold feet loses courage before an important event.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Between you and ___, the plan will fail.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Everyone should bring ___ own textbook.
questions.explanation: "Their" shows possession; it is commonly used after "everyone".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: It was ___ who broke the window.
questions.explanation: After "it was", formal English uses the subject pronoun "he".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The two friends helped each ___.
questions.explanation: "Each other" is used for two people; "one another" is often used for more than two.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: I have ___ money left, so I can't buy lunch.
questions.explanation: "Little" (without "a") means almost none; "few" is used with countable nouns.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: She is ___ honest girl.
questions.explanation: Use "an" before a vowel sound; the "h" in "honest" is silent.

questions.text: What is the plural of "child"?
questions.explanation: "Child" has an irregular plural, "children".

questions.text: What is the plural of "criterion"?
questions.explanation: "Criterion" comes from Greek, and its plural is "criteria".

questions.text: What is the plural of "mother-in-law"?
questions.explanation: The main word, "mother", takes the plural ending.

questions.text: Which of these nouns has no plural form in standard English?
questions.explanation: "Furniture" is uncountable: say "pieces of furniture".

questions.text: What is the plural of "analysis"?
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in "-is" often change to "-es": crisis → crises, thesis → theses.

questions.text: What is the plural of "phenomenon"?
questions.explanation: Like "criterion", "phenomenon" changes "-on" to "-a".

questions.text: In which word is the "b" silent?
questions.explanation: The "b" in "doubt", "debt", "lamb" and "thumb" is not pronounced.

questions.text: In which word is the "t" silent?
questions.explanation: "Listen", "castle" and "whistle" have a silent "t".

questions.text: In which word is the "w" silent?
questions.explanation: The "w" in "write", "wrist" and "wrong" is silent.

questions.text: In which word is the "h" silent?
questions.explanation: "Hour", "honest" and "heir" begin with a vowel sound.

questions.text: In which word is the "g" silent?
questions.explanation: In "sign" the "g" is silent, but in "signal" it is pronounced.

questions.text: In which word is the "l" silent?
questions.explanation: The "l" in "calm", "walk", "talk" and "half" is silent.

questions.text: Which word rhymes with "bread"?
questions.explanation: "Bread" and "said" both end in /ed/, despite the different spellings.

questions.text: Which word rhymes with "gone"?
questions.explanation: "Gone" and "on" share the vowel /ɒ/ in British English.

questions.text: Which word rhymes with "wear"?
questions.explanation: "Wear" and "chair" end with the same sound /eə/.

questions.text: Which word rhymes with "laugh"?
questions.explanation: "Laugh" and "half" both end in /ɑːf/.

questions.text: Which word rhymes with "key"?
questions.explanation: Both end in the long vowel /iː/.

questions.text: Which word rhymes with "love"?
questions.explanation: "Love" and "dove" share /ʌv/. "Move" has /uː/ and "stove" has /əʊ/.

questions.text: In the sentence "AMAKA bought the red dress", the capital letters show the stressed word. Which question does it answer?
options: Did Amaka sell the red dress?
questions.explanation: Stressing "Amaka" shows that the important information is who did it.

questions.text: In "Amaka bought the RED dress", which question is answered?
options: Did Amaka buy the red shoes?
Did Amaka borrow the red dress?
questions.explanation: The stress on "red" contrasts it with dresses of other colours.

questions.text: In "Amaka BOUGHT the red dress", which question is answered?
options: What colour was the dress Amaka bought?
Did Amaka borrow the red dress?
Did Amaka buy the red shoes?
questions.explanation: Stressing the verb contrasts buying with another action, such as borrowing.

questions.text: In "The bus left at SEVEN o'clock", which question is answered?
options: Did the car leave at seven o'clock?
Did the bus leave at six o'clock?
Did the bus arrive at seven o'clock?
questions.explanation: The stress on "seven" corrects a wrong time.

questions.text: In "My father drives a TAXI", which question is answered?
options: Does your father ride a taxi?
Does your father drive a bus?
Does your mother drive a taxi?
questions.explanation: Stressing "taxi" contrasts it with another vehicle.

questions.text: In "We are travelling to Kano TOMORROW", which question is answered?
options: Are you travelling to Kano today?
Are you travelling to Kaduna tomorrow?
Who is travelling to Kano tomorrow?
Are you flying to Kano tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Stressing "tomorrow" shows the important information is the time.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ indoors.
questions.explanation: A real (first) conditional uses "if + present" with "will".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: If I had known, I ___ you.
questions.explanation: An impossible past (third) conditional uses "had + past participle" and "would have".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: If water ___ to 100 °C, it boils.
questions.explanation: General truths (zero conditional) use the present in both clauses.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Unless you hurry, you ___ the bus.
questions.explanation: "Unless" means "if not": if you do not hurry, you will miss the bus.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Had she studied harder, she ___ the exam.
questions.explanation: "Had she studied" is an inverted form of "If she had studied".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: If I ___ a bird, I would fly home.
questions.explanation: In unreal present conditions, formal English uses "were" for all persons.

questions.text: Which prefix gives "possible" its opposite meaning?
questions.explanation: "Impossible". Before p, b and m, "in-" usually becomes "im-".

questions.text: Which prefix gives "agree" its opposite meaning?
questions.explanation: "Disagree".

questions.text: Which word is formed by adding a suffix to make a noun from "happy"?
questions.explanation: The suffix "-ness" forms a noun; "-ly" forms an adverb.

questions.text: What is the adjective form of "danger"?
questions.explanation: The suffix "-ous" forms an adjective.

questions.text: What is the verb form of "strength"?
questions.explanation: The suffix "-en" forms verbs such as "strengthen", "widen" and "shorten".

questions.text: The prefix "pre-" in "prepaid" means
questions.explanation: Prepaid means paid in advance.

questions.text: "Please close the door." What type of sentence is this?
questions.explanation: Imperative sentences give orders, requests or instructions.

questions.text: "What a beautiful day!" What type of sentence is this?
questions.explanation: Exclamatory sentences express strong feeling and end with an exclamation mark.

questions.text: A sentence with one main clause and at least one subordinate clause is a
questions.explanation: For example: "I stayed at home because I was ill."

questions.text: "I wanted to go, but it was raining." What type of sentence is this?
questions.explanation: Two main clauses are joined by the coordinating conjunction "but".

questions.text: Which of these is a simple sentence?
options: When the dog barked, we woke up.
The dog barked and the cat ran.
The dog barked because it saw a stranger.
questions.explanation: A simple sentence has only one clause.

questions.text: "Is the library open today?" What type of sentence is this?
questions.explanation: Interrogative sentences ask questions.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: By next year, I ___ in this school for five years.
questions.explanation: The future perfect shows a duration completed by a future time.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: She ___ her homework before her mother came home.
questions.explanation: The past perfect shows the earlier of two past actions.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Water ___ at 100 °C at sea level.
questions.explanation: Scientific facts use the simple present.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Mathematics ___ my best subject.
questions.explanation: Subjects ending in "-ics" such as Mathematics and Physics take a singular verb.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: A number of students ___ absent today.
questions.explanation: "A number of" means "many" and takes a plural verb.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The committee ___ divided in their opinions.
questions.explanation: When the members act as individuals ("their opinions"), the collective noun takes a plural verb.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: He has been ill ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: "Since" is used with a point in time; "for" is used with a period of time.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The thief broke ___ the house at night.
questions.explanation: To "break into" a building means to enter it by force.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: She is married ___ a doctor.
questions.explanation: The correct expression is "married to".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The students were asked to hand ___ their assignments.
questions.explanation: To "hand in" means to submit.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "pleasant" in this sentence: The weather was pleasant all week.
questions.explanation: "Pleasant" means enjoyable or nice, which is what "agreeable" means.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "diligent" in this sentence: Ada is a diligent student.
questions.explanation: A diligent person works carefully and steadily, so "hardworking" is closest.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "commence" in this sentence: The exam will commence at 9 a.m.
questions.explanation: "Commence" is a formal word for "begin".

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "abundant" in this sentence: Rainfall is abundant in the south.
questions.explanation: "Abundant" means existing in large quantities, so "plentiful" is closest.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "obstinate" in this sentence: The obstinate boy refused to apologise.
questions.explanation: An obstinate person refuses to change their mind, which is being stubborn.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "vital" in this sentence: Water is vital to life.
questions.explanation: "Vital" means absolutely necessary, which is what "essential" means.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "reluctant" in this sentence: Emeka was reluctant to lend his phone.
questions.explanation: To be reluctant is to be unwilling or hesitant to do something.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "generous" in this sentence: Mr Bello is a generous man.
questions.explanation: A generous person gives freely; a stingy person is unwilling to give.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "ancient" in this sentence: Benin has many ancient walls.
questions.explanation: "Ancient" means very old, so its opposite is "modern".

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "victory" in this sentence: The team celebrated its victory.
questions.explanation: A victory is a win; the opposite is a defeat.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "permanent" in this sentence: She got a permanent job.
questions.explanation: "Permanent" means lasting for a long time; "temporary" means lasting only a short time.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "humble" in this sentence: Despite his success, Tunde remained humble.
questions.explanation: A humble person does not boast; an arrogant person thinks they are better than others.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "scarce" in this sentence: Fuel was scarce last month.
questions.explanation: "Scarce" means in short supply; "plentiful" means available in large amounts.

questions.text: What does "to burn the midnight oil" mean?
options: to study or work late into the night
to start a fire at night
questions.explanation: The idiom describes someone working or studying until very late.

questions.text: What does "a piece of cake" mean?
questions.explanation: If a task is "a piece of cake", it is very easy to do.

questions.text: What does "to let the cat out of the bag" mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means to reveal information that was meant to be kept secret.

questions.text: What does "to hit the nail on the head" mean?
questions.explanation: When you hit the nail on the head, you say exactly the right thing about a situation.

questions.text: The teacher told the class to "hold their horses". What did she mean?
questions.explanation: "Hold your horses" means to wait and not rush into something.

questions.text: What does "once in a blue moon" mean?
questions.explanation: Something that happens once in a blue moon happens very rarely.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ in the hall.
questions.explanation: With "neither … nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject. "Students" is plural, so "were" is correct.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Each of the boys ___ a uniform.
questions.explanation: "Each" is singular, so it takes the singular verb "has".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The news ___ very encouraging.
questions.explanation: "News" is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Bread and butter ___ my favourite breakfast.
questions.explanation: "Bread and butter" is treated as one dish, so it takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The principal, together with his staff, ___ arrived.
questions.explanation: Phrases like "together with" do not change the subject. The subject "principal" is singular.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The number of students in the class ___ increasing.
questions.explanation: "The number of" is singular. ("A number of" would take a plural verb.)

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: By the time we got to the stadium, the match ___.
questions.explanation: The past perfect "had started" shows an action completed before another past action.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: She ___ in Lagos since 2019.
questions.explanation: "Since" with a time that continues to now takes the present perfect.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: If I were you, I ___ apologise.
questions.explanation: An unreal condition ("If I were…") takes "would" in the main clause.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Every morning, my father ___ to work.
questions.explanation: The simple present describes habits and routines.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: While I was reading, the light ___ out.
questions.explanation: A short action interrupting a longer one in the past takes the simple past.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Look at those dark clouds! It ___ rain.
questions.explanation: "Going to" is used for predictions based on present evidence.

questions.text: What part of speech is "quickly" in this sentence: She ran quickly to the gate.
questions.explanation: "Quickly" tells us how she ran, so it modifies a verb. It is an adverb.

questions.text: What part of speech is "beautiful" in this sentence: Calabar is a beautiful city.
questions.explanation: "Beautiful" describes the noun "city", so it is an adjective.

questions.text: What part of speech is "under" in this sentence: The cat is under the table.
questions.explanation: "Under" shows the relationship between "cat" and "table", so it is a preposition.

questions.text: What part of speech is "although" in this sentence: Although it rained, we played football.
questions.explanation: "Although" joins two clauses, so it is a conjunction.

questions.text: What part of speech is "honesty" in this sentence: Honesty is the best policy.
questions.explanation: "Honesty" names a quality, so it is an abstract noun.

questions.text: What part of speech is "themselves" in this sentence: The girls prepared the meal themselves.
questions.explanation: "Themselves" is a reflexive (emphatic) pronoun.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: She is good ___ Mathematics.
questions.explanation: The correct expression is "good at" a subject or skill.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The students were congratulated ___ their success.
questions.explanation: We congratulate someone "on" an achievement.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Please look ___ the word in your dictionary.
questions.explanation: To "look up" a word means to search for it in a reference book.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The meeting has been put ___ until next week.
questions.explanation: To "put off" means to postpone.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: My grandmother looks ___ the children when we travel.
questions.explanation: To "look after" someone means to take care of them.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: He was accused ___ stealing the money.
questions.explanation: The correct expression is "accused of" something.

questions.text: Choose the correct question tag: You are coming to the party, ___?
questions.explanation: A positive statement takes a negative tag with the same auxiliary: "are" → "aren't you".

questions.text: Choose the correct question tag: She can't swim, ___?
questions.explanation: A negative statement takes a positive tag: "can't" → "can she".

questions.text: Choose the correct question tag: They went to Abuja yesterday, ___?
questions.explanation: The simple past "went" uses the auxiliary "did", so the negative tag is "didn't they".

questions.text: Choose the correct question tag: Let's start the lesson, ___?
questions.explanation: Sentences beginning with "Let's" take the tag "shall we".

questions.text: Choose the correct question tag: Nobody called me, ___?
questions.explanation: "Nobody" makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive, and it uses "they".

questions.text: Choose the correct question tag: I am your friend, ___?
questions.explanation: The standard tag for "I am" is "aren't I".

questions.text: Identify the type of clause in brackets: I know [that he is honest].
questions.explanation: The clause is the object of "know", so it does the work of a noun.

questions.text: Identify the type of clause in brackets: The man [who sold us the car] has travelled.
questions.explanation: The clause describes the noun "man", so it is an adjective (relative) clause.

questions.text: Identify the type of clause in brackets: We stayed indoors [because it was raining].
questions.explanation: The clause tells us why we stayed indoors.

questions.text: Identify the type of clause in brackets: [When the bell rang], the students left.
questions.explanation: The clause tells us when the students left.

questions.text: Identify the type of clause in brackets: [If you study hard], you will pass.
questions.explanation: "If" introduces a condition.

questions.text: What is the grammatical name of "in the morning" in this sentence: We leave in the morning.
questions.explanation: It has no finite verb, so it is a phrase. It tells us when, so it is adverbial.

questions.text: Choose the correct reported form: He said, "I am tired."
options: He said that he is being tired.
He said that he had been tiring.
He said that he was tired.
He said that I am tired.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, "I" becomes "he" and "am" moves back to "was".

questions.text: Choose the correct reported form: She said, "I will call you tomorrow."
options: She said that she would call me the next day.
She said that she will call me tomorrow.
She said that she called me the next day.
She said that I would call her tomorrow.
questions.explanation: "Will" becomes "would" and "tomorrow" becomes "the next day".

questions.text: Choose the correct reported form: The teacher asked, "Have you finished?"
options: The teacher asked if we had finished.
The teacher asked if we have finished.
The teacher asked have we finished.
The teacher asked that had we finished.
questions.explanation: Yes/no questions are reported with "if" or "whether", and "have finished" becomes "had finished".

questions.text: Choose the correct reported form: Mother said to me, "Close the door."
options: Mother told me to close the door.
Mother said me to close the door.
Mother told me that close the door.
Mother told me I closed the door.
questions.explanation: Commands are reported with "told + person + to + verb".

questions.text: Choose the correct reported form: Musa said, "I bought this phone yesterday."
options: Musa said that he had bought that phone the day before.
Musa said that he bought this phone yesterday.
Musa said that he has bought this phone yesterday.
Musa said that I had bought that phone the day before.
questions.explanation: The simple past moves back to the past perfect, "this" becomes "that" and "yesterday" becomes "the day before".

questions.text: Choose the correct reported form: Bisi asked, "Where do you live?"
options: Bisi asked where do I live.
Bisi asked where did I live.
Bisi asked that where I lived.
questions.explanation: In reported questions the word order becomes a statement, and the tense moves back.

questions.text: Choose the passive form of: The boy kicked the ball.
options: The boy was kicked by the ball.
The ball is kicked by the boy.
The ball was kicked by the boy.
The ball has been kicking the boy.
questions.explanation: The object becomes the subject, and the past tense uses "was" + past participle.

questions.text: Choose the passive form of: They are building a new school.
options: A new school is being built.
questions.explanation: The present continuous passive is "is being" + past participle.

questions.text: Choose the passive form of: Someone has stolen my bag.
options: My bag is stolen by someone has.
questions.explanation: The present perfect passive is "has been" + past participle.

questions.text: Choose the active form of: The letter was written by Ngozi.
questions.explanation: The agent "Ngozi" becomes the subject, and the tense stays in the simple past.

questions.text: Choose the passive form of: The principal will announce the results.
options: The results will be announced by the principal.
The results are announced by the principal.
The results will announce the principal.
The results would be announced by the principal.
questions.explanation: The future passive is "will be" + past participle.

questions.text: In which sentence is the verb in the passive voice?
options: She cleans her room every day.
questions.explanation: "Were cleaned" is "be" + past participle, and the subject receives the action.

questions.text: Which word has the same vowel sound as "seat"?
questions.explanation: "Seat" and "key" both have the long vowel /iː/. "Sit" has the short /ɪ/.

questions.text: Which word has the same vowel sound as "food"?
questions.explanation: "Food" and "blue" both have /uː/. "Good" and "foot" have /ʊ/, and "flood" has /ʌ/.

questions.text: Which word has the same vowel sound as "cat"?
questions.explanation: "Cat" and "man" both have /æ/.

questions.text: Which word contains a diphthong?
questions.explanation: "Boy" has /ɔɪ/, a glide from one vowel to another. The others have single (pure) vowels.

questions.text: Which word has the same vowel sound as "bird"?
questions.explanation: "Bird" and "word" both have the long vowel /ɜː/.

questions.text: Which word has the same vowel sound as "cup"?
questions.explanation: "Cup" and "love" both have /ʌ/, even though they are spelt differently.

questions.text: Which word begins with the same consonant sound as "think"?
questions.explanation: "Think" and "thumb" begin with the voiceless /θ/. "This" begins with the voiced /ð/.

questions.text: Which word begins with the same consonant sound as "she"?
questions.explanation: "Sugar" begins with /ʃ/, the same sound as "sh" in "she".

questions.text: In which word is the "ch" pronounced /k/?
questions.explanation: In "chemistry", "ch" is pronounced /k/. In the others it is /tʃ/.

questions.text: In which word is the first letter silent?
questions.explanation: The "k" in "knee" is not pronounced.

questions.text: Which word ends with the sound /z/?
questions.explanation: The plural "-s" is pronounced /z/ after voiced sounds such as /g/.

questions.text: Which word contains the sound /ʒ/?
questions.explanation: The "s" in "measure" is /ʒ/, as in "pleasure" and "vision".

questions.text: Which word is stressed on the second syllable?
questions.explanation: be-GIN is stressed on the second syllable. The others are stressed on the first.

questions.text: Which word is stressed on the first syllable?
questions.explanation: MAR-ket is stressed on the first syllable.

questions.text: "Record" can be a noun or a verb. As a verb, which syllable is stressed?
questions.explanation: Many two-syllable words are stressed on the first syllable as nouns and on the second as verbs.

questions.text: Which word is stressed on the third syllable?
questions.explanation: un-der-STAND is stressed on the third syllable.

questions.text: Which word is stressed on the second syllable?
questions.explanation: im-POR-tant is stressed on the second syllable. The others are stressed on the first.

questions.text: Which word has a different stress pattern from the others?
questions.explanation: de-CIDE is stressed on the second syllable; the other three are stressed on the first.

questions.text: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: "Necessary" has one "c" and double "s".

questions.text: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: "Accommodation" has double "c" and double "m".

questions.text: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Remember "i before e, except after c": receive.

questions.text: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: There is "a rat" in "separate".

questions.text: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: "Committee" has double "m", double "t" and double "e".

questions.text: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: "Occurrence" has double "c", double "r" and ends in "-ence".

questions.text: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
questions.explanation: A question starts with a capital letter and ends with a question mark.

questions.text: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
questions.explanation: For a plural noun ending in "s", the apostrophe comes after the "s": girls'.

questions.text: Which option correctly uses "its"?
options: The dog wagged it is tail.
questions.explanation: "Its" (no apostrophe) shows possession. "It's" means "it is".

questions.text: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
options: I bought rice, beans, yam and oil.
I bought, rice beans yam and oil.
I bought rice beans, yam, and, oil.
I, bought rice beans yam and oil.
questions.explanation: Commas separate items in a list.

questions.text: Which punctuation mark introduces a list after a complete sentence?
questions.explanation: A colon (:) introduces a list or explanation, e.g. "You need three things: a pen, a ruler and a pencil."

questions.text: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
questions.explanation: The comma comes inside the closing quotation mark when the quote is followed by the speaker.

questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: The classroom was as quiet as a graveyard.
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using "as" or "like".

questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: Time is a thief.
questions.explanation: A metaphor says one thing is another without using "like" or "as".

questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: The wind whispered through the trees.
questions.explanation: Giving a human action (whispering) to a non-human thing is personification.

questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: I have told you a million times!
questions.explanation: Hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration for effect.

questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: The bees buzzed around the flowers.
questions.explanation: "Buzzed" imitates the sound it describes.

questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers.
questions.explanation: Alliteration is the repetition of the same consonant sound at the start of nearby words.

questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: His grandfather passed away last year.
questions.explanation: "Passed away" is a gentler way of saying "died".

questions.text: Which group of words belongs to the register of medicine?
questions.explanation: These words are used in hospitals and health care.

questions.text: Which group of words belongs to the register of law?
questions.explanation: These words are used in courts and legal practice.

questions.text: In which field would you hear "headline", "editor" and "column"?
questions.explanation: These are words used by newspapers and the media.

questions.text: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The bank charged him interest on the ___ he took to start his business.
questions.explanation: Interest is charged on money borrowed, which is a loan.

questions.text: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The farmer used a ___ to remove the weeds.
questions.explanation: A hoe is a farming tool used for weeding and digging.

questions.text: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: After the final whistle, the ___ showed the player a red card.
questions.explanation: In football, the referee controls the match and shows cards.

questions.text: Which of these letters needs the writer's address and the receiver's address?
options: an informal letter to a friend
questions.explanation: A formal (official) letter has two addresses: the writer's and the recipient's.

questions.text: Which is the best closing for a formal letter that begins "Dear Sir"?
questions.explanation: "Yours faithfully" is used when the letter begins with "Dear Sir" or "Dear Madam".

questions.text: Which kind of essay mainly tells a story of events?
questions.explanation: A narrative essay recounts events, usually in the order they happened.

questions.text: Which kind of essay tries to persuade the reader to accept one side of an issue?
questions.explanation: An argumentative essay presents points for one side to convince the reader.

questions.text: In an informal letter, where should the date be written?
options: at the end of the letter
questions.explanation: The date goes directly below the writer's address at the top right.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a summary?
options: to copy the passage in full
to add new examples to the passage
to state the main points briefly in your own words
to give your opinion on the passage
questions.explanation: A summary gives only the main points, briefly and in your own words.

questions.text: If f(x) = 2x + 3, find f(4).
If f(x) = x² and g(x) = x + 1, find f(g(2)).
questions.explanation: g(2) = 3, and f(3) = 9. (g(f(2)) would be 5.)

questions.text: Find the inverse of f(x) = 3x − 2.
questions.explanation: Let y = 3x − 2. Then x = (y + 2)/3, so f⁻¹(x) = (x + 2)/3.

questions.text: For what value of x is f(x) = 1/(x − 3) undefined?
questions.explanation: Division by zero is undefined, and x − 3 = 0 when x = 3.

questions.text: A function that is both one-to-one and onto is called
questions.explanation: A bijection pairs every element of the domain with exactly one element of the codomain, and vice versa.

questions.text: f(x) = x² − 1 has domain {−1, 0, 1}. Find its range.
questions.explanation: f(−1) = 0, f(0) = −1 and f(1) = 0, so the range is {−1, 0}.

questions.text: What is the negation of "It is raining"?
questions.explanation: The negation simply denies the statement.

questions.text: The implication p ⇒ q is false only when
options: both p and q are true
p is true and q is false
both p and q are false
p is false and q is true
questions.explanation: A true condition leading to a false result breaks the implication.

questions.text: What is the contrapositive of "If it rains, the ground is wet"?
options: If the ground is wet, then it rained.
It rains and the ground is not wet.
If the ground is not wet, then it did not rain.
If it does not rain, the ground is not wet.
questions.explanation: The contrapositive of p ⇒ q is ~q ⇒ ~p. It is equivalent to the original statement.

questions.text: The conjunction p ∧ q is true when
options: either p or q is true
neither p nor q is true
both p and q are true
questions.explanation: "And" requires both parts to be true.

questions.text: What is the converse of "If a figure is a square, then it is a rectangle"?
options: If a figure is not a square, then it is not a rectangle.
If a figure is a rectangle, then it is a square.
If a figure is not a rectangle, then it is not a square.
A figure is a square and not a rectangle.
questions.explanation: The converse of p ⇒ q is q ⇒ p. Here the converse is false even though the statement is true.

questions.text: The disjunction p ∨ q is false when
options: both p and q are false
both p and q are true

questions.text: Who was the first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature?
questions.explanation: Soyinka won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986.

questions.text: In "Things Fall Apart", Okonkwo's greatest fear is
options: being seen as weak like his father, Unoka
losing his farm to the white men
questions.explanation: Okonkwo's fear of weakness drives many of his harsh actions.

questions.text: Which Nigerian playwright wrote "The Gods Are Not to Blame"?
questions.explanation: Ola Rotimi's play is an adaptation of Sophocles' "Oedipus Rex".

questions.text: Négritude was a literary movement that
questions.explanation: Writers such as Léopold Senghor promoted pride in African heritage.

questions.text: The title "Things Fall Apart" is taken from a poem by
questions.explanation: The line comes from Yeats's poem "The Second Coming".

questions.text: In Shakespeare's "Macbeth", who persuades Macbeth to murder King Duncan?
questions.explanation: Lady Macbeth questions Macbeth's courage and pushes him to kill Duncan.

questions.text: In "Macbeth", the witches' prophecy first tells Macbeth that he will become
questions.explanation: The witches hail him as Thane of Glamis, Thane of Cawdor and future king.

questions.text: Shakespeare's "Romeo and Juliet" is best described as a
questions.explanation: The young lovers both die at the end.

questions.text: In "Julius Caesar", who says "Et tu, Brute?"
questions.explanation: Caesar says it as he sees his friend Brutus among his attackers.

questions.text: Shakespeare's plays were mainly written during the reign of
options: Queen Elizabeth I and King James I
questions.explanation: Shakespeare wrote between about 1590 and 1613.

questions.text: Shakespeare's "Othello" is the story of
options: a Scottish king who loses his throne
two young lovers from rival families
a prince who avenges his father
a general destroyed by jealousy stirred up by Iago
questions.explanation: Iago deceives Othello into believing that Desdemona is unfaithful.

questions.text: The attitude of a writer towards the subject is the
questions.explanation: Tone may be angry, humorous, bitter, sympathetic and so on.

questions.text: The feeling that a work creates in the reader is the
questions.explanation: Mood is the atmosphere the reader experiences.

questions.text: A writer's choice of words is called
questions.explanation: Diction can be formal, informal, simple or elevated.

questions.text: Language that appeals to the senses is called
questions.explanation: Imagery helps the reader see, hear, smell, taste or feel what is described.

questions.text: A character who changes and develops during a story is a
questions.explanation: Round characters are complex and grow; flat characters stay the same.

questions.text: The use of an object or person to stand for an idea is
questions.explanation: For example, a dove may symbolise peace.

questions.text: Convert 1101₂ to a base 10 number.
Convert 25 (base 10) to base 2.

questions.text: Find 17 (mod 5).
questions.explanation: 17 = 3×5 + 2, so the remainder is 2.

questions.text: Evaluate (8 + 9) mod 6.
questions.explanation: 8 + 9 = 17, and 17 = 2×6 + 5, so the answer is 5.

questions.text: Evaluate 7 × 8 (mod 9).

questions.text: Solve x + 4 ≡ 2 (mod 7).
Today is Monday. What day of the week will it be in 30 days?
questions.explanation: 30 = 4×7 + 2, so it is 2 days after Monday: Wednesday.

questions.text: Solve 3x ≡ 1 (mod 5).
Simplify 2³ × 2⁴.

questions.text: Evaluate 27^(2/3).

questions.text: Simplify a⁵ ÷ a².

questions.text: Evaluate 5⁰ + 4⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1, and 4⁻¹ = ¼. So 1 + ¼ = 1¼.

questions.text: Solve 2ˣ = 32.

questions.text: Evaluate 16^(−1/2).
questions.explanation: 16^(1/2) = 4, and the negative index means the reciprocal, so the answer is ¼.

questions.text: Evaluate log₁₀ 1000.
Evaluate log₂ 8.

questions.text: Simplify log₁₀ 5 + log₁₀ 2.
questions.explanation: log 5 + log 2 = log (5 × 2) = log₁₀ 10 = 1.

questions.text: If log₃ x = 4, find x.
questions.explanation: log₃ x = 4 means x = 3⁴ = 81.

questions.text: Evaluate log₂ 32 − log₂ 4.
questions.explanation: log₂ 32 − log₂ 4 = log₂ (32 ÷ 4) = log₂ 8 = 3.

questions.text: Write 2 log 3 + log 4 as a single logarithm.
